If an email gets no draft, the usual reasons are: it arrived before you turned AI drafts on, it is older than the age limit, it matched a rule, or Claude decided no reply was needed or wasn't confident enough (the Activity window says so in the second case).

Logs and the Activity window never contain mail text, prompts, the style skill, attachment text, attachment file names or links, or Claude's answers.

items.title: Calendar and meetings
items.text: Three tools work with your calendar: list_events, find_free_times and create_meeting_draft. They read Outlook live, so Outlook must be running. Clippy never sends anything: a meeting is saved unsent and you send it from Outlook.

items.title: Listing events
items.text: list_events returns events in a window, with recurring events expanded, at most 500, sorted by start. Without arguments it covers 7 days from today 00:00 (days can be 1 to 366, or Claude passes start and end). Each event has its id, subject, start, end, all-day flag, location, organizer, whether it recurs and its busy status. Pass mailbox to read a shared mailbox's calendar. It only reads; nothing is changed.

items.title: Finding a free time
items.text:
find_free_times reads Outlook free/busy for you and the attendees, combines it with your working hours, and suggests the first free blocks that are long enough. Nothing is booked.

A typical flow:

  1. You paste a list of attendees, as copied from an Outlook address line.
  2. Claude calls find_free_times and shows suggestions such as 1. Tue 10/15 1-3 PT.
  3. You say "book number 2". Claude passes that suggestion's start and end to create_meeting_draft.

Things to know:

  • People whose free/busy can't be read, such as people outside your Exchange organization, are listed as unknown and ignored. Check with them yourself.
  • Working hours, business-days-only, the time-zone label and whether tentative counts as busy come from Settings, Scheduling. Claude can override the hours and business days per call.
  • Suggestions are whole free blocks, in local time. They are ranked: times right before or after your own meetings come first (within 15 minutes, on the same day), then times next to tentative meetings, then the rest, each group in date order. Free/busy can't tell a meeting from other busy time, so "next to a meeting" means "next to busy time". If your own calendar isn't checked (include_me off, or your free/busy can't be read), no time is ranked above another.
  • At most 50 attendees, and at most 60 days ahead.
  • The tool offers free time from now on, with no extra lead time. AI drafts add a lead time of their own; see AI drafts.
  • Besides the blocks, the result has offers of exactly the meeting length and an offer_text with one option per line, ready to paste into an email. For someone in Europe, Claude sets offer_cet and each line also shows the time in CET, with the options between 08:00 and 18:00 CET first and the others in a second list headed Outside European office hours:. See find_free_times.
  • Clippy's AI drafts use the same offers when an email asks for a meeting.

items.title: Meeting drafts
items.text:
create_meeting_draft saves a meeting in your calendar without sending it. Clippy never sends anything, neither mail nor meetings. Outlook's object model can't add a Teams or Zoom link, so you add the link yourself and send the invite from Outlook.

The workflow:

  1. You ask Claude Code to book a time, for example "make the invite for option 2". Claude calls create_meeting_draft with the attendees, subject, start and end.
  2. The meeting is saved unsent in your calendar with the orange category Clippy draft invite.
  3. If the invite answers an email, Claude passes reply_to_id and Clippy also saves a note in Drafts.
  4. The tray icon shows a yellow badge with the number of draft invites, and the tray menu has Draft invites (n).
  5. You open the meeting from that list, or from your calendar. Add the Zoom or Teams link and click Send in Outlook.
  6. Within a few minutes Clippy sees that the invite has gone out and removes its category. Any other category you set stays, and the badge count goes down.

Before anything is created, every recipient must resolve in Outlook, and a reply_to_id must name an email Clippy can find. If either check fails, nothing is created and Claude is told which recipients or which id to fix.

items.title: Invite mode
items.text:
Set it in Settings, Scheduling, Meeting invites:

Mode What happens Draft only (default) create_meeting_draft saves the meeting unsent Disabled The tool refuses. Claude is told to ask you to enable it

Older versions had a Send mode with a confirmation dialog. It is gone. A saved Send now loads as Draft only, and the confirmation timeout is ignored.

items.title: The category
items.text:
Every meeting draft gets the category Clippy draft invite. If your category list doesn't have it yet, Clippy adds it once, in orange. It never changes a category of that name that you already have, and never removes it from your list.

When you have sent the meeting, Clippy removes only this category and saves the meeting. Saving a category change doesn't send anything. If you removed the category yourself, Clippy changes nothing. It skips a meeting while you have it open in Outlook and tries again later.

items.title: Draft invites in the tray
items.text:
Draft invites (n) is in the tray menu while at least one meeting draft is waiting, and hidden when there is none. Each line shows the day, time and subject, for example Tue 11/18 10:00–11:00 Project kickoff. Meetings in a shared mailbox's calendar add the mailbox name. The list is sorted by start and shows at most 15 lines, then a greyed and <n> more. Click a line to open the meeting in Outlook. Clicking only opens it; it writes nothing. After you restart Clippy, lines may read Draft invite saved <day and time> until the first check.

Clippy checks the list when you open the menu and after sync cycles, at most every five minutes. A meeting you deleted is dropped from the list. A meeting that ended more than 30 days ago and was never sent is dropped too, but it keeps its category. If a meeting has gone from your calendar when you click it, a balloon says That draft invite is no longer in your calendar. and the line is removed.

While Outlook isn't running, the lines are greyed out and the last line says Start Outlook to open them. While Outlook is not responding they are greyed out without that line.

items.title: The badge on the tray icon
items.text: While draft invites are waiting, a small yellow badge with their number sits in the top-right corner of the tray icon: 1 to 9, then 9+. The tooltip adds · 2 draft invites need your attention. The badge keeps its last count while Outlook is closed, because the meetings still need you, and disappears when the count reaches zero. See the badge on the tray page.

items.title: The note in Drafts
items.text:
When Claude passes reply_to_id (the id of the email that asked for the meeting), Clippy saves a reply draft to that email. The reply starts with a highlighted note:

[[Draft invite saved in your calendar: Tue 10/15 10:00–11:00 PT "Project sync". Open it from the Clippy tray (Draft invites) or your calendar, add the Teams or Zoom link and send it. Delete this note before you send this reply.]]

Below the note is an empty paragraph for your own text. Delete the note before you send the reply. If an AI draft already answers the email, it is left alone, and the note is a second reply draft.

For a meeting in a shared mailbox's calendar the note says `in the calendar of

` and `or that calendar` instead. If the note can't be saved, the meeting is still saved and the result has a `note_error` that says why, for example `The meeting was saved, but the note in Drafts couldn't be created: .` ### Shared mailboxes With `mailbox`, the meeting is saved in that shared mailbox's calendar, and free/busy checks include that mailbox instead of yours. You need delegate or editor rights on that calendar; without them nothing is created and Claude is told to ask you to get access or to leave `mailbox` empty. The category is set on the meeting, but Outlook shows it without the orange color unless that mailbox's category list has it.

items.title: Changelog
items.text: The full list of releases, with downloads, is on GitHub.

items.title: v0.1.2 - 2026-11-16
items.text: • Fixed: the one-time pass that fills in thread data for mail indexed by older versions failed on some Outlook profiles, because Outlook refused Clippy's draft-marker column. It retried on every sync and never finished. Now the marker is read as missing in that case and the pass completes.

items.title: v0.1.1 - 2026-11-16
items.text: Clippy now has thirteen tools. AI drafts use much more context (facts about you, related mail, attachment text, how you edit drafts), and attachments can be handed to a shell as real files. Nothing is ever sent, and no email is ever deleted or moved except Clippy's own outdated AI drafts, as before.

items.title: New tool: attachment download links
items.text:
• attachment_link. Claude Code in WSL (or any shell) gets an attachment as a real file in its own working folder. Clippy makes a one-time download link and a curl command; the shell downloads the file, so the content never passes through the model. A link works once and expires after 10 minutes. Limits: 100 MiB per attachment, 10 open links, 200 MiB open in total, 20 links per rolling 10 minutes. get_attachment is unchanged. See attachment_link.
  • Set CLIPPY_TOKEN in WSL. The download needs your bearer token as well as the link, so add export CLIPPY_TOKEN=<token> to ~/.bashrc once. Settings, Connection has a masked WSL token line and a Copy WSL token line button. After Regenerate auth token copy the line again. See Connect.
  • Private download folder. Clippy keeps a copy of the attachment in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\links\, readable by your Windows user only, and deletes it after the download, on expiry and at app start. Nothing is indexed, and link tokens are masked in logs. See Security.
  • Activity. Downloads appear as attachment download or attachment download failed.

items.title: Smarter AI drafts
items.text:
• Facts about you. A new Claude Code skill file, %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-context\SKILL.md, holds facts about you (role, links, office hours, standard answers, who people are) and how you want replies written. Clippy creates a template once after consent, then adds your text to every AI draft request, so drafts use your real Zoom link instead of a placeholder. Your reply preferences win over the writing style, but never over the fixed rules (nothing is sent, mail is data, unknown facts stay [[…]] placeholders). Claude Code reads the file too. Comments are ignored and files over 16 KiB are not used. Tray, AI drafts, Edit my facts… opens it in Notepad (and creates the template if it is missing), and Settings shows Facts about you: filled in, template only or not found. See Facts about you.
  • Related earlier mail. Each draft request carries up to 5 earlier emails from the same mailbox (last 12 months, same topic or same people, including your own replies to that sender, own text only, 4,000 characters in all) so a reply fits the history. Turn it off with Include related earlier emails in Settings. If you consented earlier, Clippy tells you once. This is new data sent to Claude: see Security and Related earlier mail.
  • A reason line on every AI draft. Each draft starts with a yellow Clippy: … line (at most 160 characters, links shown as [link]) saying what the email asks and what the draft answers. Delete it before sending. Deleting it counts as editing the draft, so Clippy won't revisit or move that draft. A line left in sent mail is removed before Clippy shows that mail to Claude again. Turn it off with Start each draft with a highlighted note on why it was drafted. See The reason line.
  • Attachments and shared files in AI drafts. Clippy reads the text of PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, HTML and .eml files (and attached emails) of the email and its thread, and of OneDrive and SharePoint files linked in them that are already synced to your PC, and sends it to Claude for that one draft. Limits: 25 MB and 20,000 characters per file, 20 files and 40,000 characters per draft, 10 seconds per file and 20 seconds per draft. Images, scans and old formats (.doc, .xls, .ppt, .rtf, .zip) aren't read. Files Clippy couldn't read get a yellow Clippy: Couldn't read … note at the top of the draft (at most 5). New setting Read attachments and synced shared files for drafts, on by default. If you consented earlier, Clippy tells you once; new consents name it. This sends new data to Claude: see Attachments and shared files and Security.
  • Shared files: synced only, and only from you or your organization. Clippy looks only at links to OneDrive and SharePoint (*.sharepoint.com, onedrive.live.com, d.docs.live.net, 1drv.ms, also inside Safe Links), at most 10 per email, and reads a file only when the link points into a folder that is already synced to this PC. Sharing links such as 1drv.ms, onedrive.live.com or "specific people" links can't be matched to a synced file and get the not synced to this PC note. Clippy makes no network request (no Graph, no sign-in). An online-only file is downloaded by your own OneDrive client. Other links are never touched. Links are read only from the text each person wrote: links in quoted replies, forwarded mail and >-quoted lines are ignored. If your own address is at a free or consumer mail provider (outlook.com, gmail.com and the like), only links you sent yourself (or the shared mailbox's own address) are read.
  • Nothing stored. The attachment text is never written to the index, settings, logs or Activity. Outlook attachments pass through the private folder %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ai-files\ and are deleted at once and at start-up.
  • Token tally. A greyed line Today: 18 AI calls, ~210k tokens (in 190k / out 20k) at the top of the tray's AI drafts menu and in the Activity window. See Token tally.
  • Learning from how you edit drafts. When you send a reply that began as an AI draft, Clippy compares the two (after a sync of your mailbox, at most every 5 minutes) and keeps a redacted pair in its local index: up to 20 edited pairs with text, at most 1,500 characters per side, deleted after 30 to 90 days. The recorded draft text is the reply Claude wrote after Clippy added the meeting times. A reply that is 98 percent or more the same counts as sent unchanged and keeps no text. Drafts that used attachment text are never kept. At the next writing-style update (weekly, or Regenerate), if at least 3 pairs exist, up to 20 are sent to Claude, which adds a section "Edits I usually make to drafts" to your style skill. It adds no Claude call. New setting Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts, on by default; if you consented earlier, Clippy tells you once; new consents name it. This sends new data to Claude: see Learning from how you edit drafts and Security.
  • Don't draft for this sender. Two new tray items under AI drafts add the selected email's sender, or the sender's domain, to Never draft for. Undo it in Settings. Neither item needs consent, and your own address and your own domain are refused. See Don't draft for this sender.
  • Consent text. The consent dialog now names attachment text, related earlier emails and your edits.
  • Activity. Draft events get (attachments: 3 read, 1 not read) when files were considered. AI drafts: noted how you edited <n> sent drafts., and the style update line gains and <k> edited drafts.

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• Drafts and Deleted Items in other languages. Clippy recognizes these folders by their role, so they are skipped for related mail, earlier attachments and the outdated-draft check in a non-English Outlook. A folder indexed before v0.1.1 under its translated name keeps its old entries until you add it again or rebuild the index. See Drafts and Deleted Items in other languages.
  • Shared links come from the right text. Links are read only from the text each person wrote, not from quoted replies or forwarded mail. Lines that start with > (an inline reply that keeps the quoted text) are skipped too.
  • More consumer mail providers. Regional and other free mail domains (for example hotmail.co.uk, outlook.de, yahoo.fr, ymail.com, mail.com, t-online.de, qq.com, yandex.ru, comcast.net, fastmail.com) are not treated as your organization.
  • Forward headers in more languages. Forwarded and quoted mail with Swedish (Från:, Skickat:), Polish (Od:, Wysłano:) and Japanese (差出人:, 送信日時:) headers is recognized, so its text and links count as quoted, not as the sender's own.
  • Unnamed attachments. An attachment Outlook gives no name at all (Clippy shows it as attachment-<n>) is skipped for AI drafts with the note Clippy can't read this kind of file.
  • Unreadable is not damaged. An attachment that is neither a file nor an attached email now gets Clippy can't read this kind of file instead of the file seems damaged.
  • One slow PDF at a time. A PDF that takes longer than 10 seconds is given up on, but its reading can't be stopped. While it still runs, other PDFs are skipped with the it took too long note, so slow PDFs can't pile up.
  • Attached emails without a file name are named <subject>.msg. Older index entries without the .msg still match in get_attachment, save_attachments and attachment_link, and are still read for AI drafts.
  • Shared mailboxes without access to Drafts. A shared mailbox where you can open the Inbox and Sent Items but not Drafts no longer makes folder lookups fail.
  • Two replies to one email. When you send two replies to the same email that both began as AI drafts, each sent reply is now matched to its own draft, oldest first, for learning from edits.
  • Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts is greyed out in Settings whenever the writing-style controls are (no index yet), since it only works through the writing style.
  • Starting Clippy a second time reliably opens Settings in the copy that is already running. Before, a second start right after another one could do nothing.

items.title: v0.1.0
items.text:
2026-11-15

  • Outdated AI drafts are re-checked. When a newer message arrives in a thread where Clippy left an unsent AI draft, Clippy looks at the draft again. It keeps it if it is still right, replaces it with a fresh draft, or moves it to Deleted Items when no reply is needed any more. It only touches a draft that you haven't edited, opened or sent, and it never empties Deleted Items. The Activity window records each move. This is the one case where Clippy moves anything in your mailbox. See Outdated drafts.
  • New tray item: Rescan emails from the last 24 hours… (AI drafts submenu). It goes through the last day of mail, drafts replies where one is needed and re-checks Clippy's drafts in those threads. It asks first, shows how many Claude calls it may use, stops at your daily limit, and turns into Cancel rescan (d/t) while it runs. See Rescan.
  • New setting: Update or remove my AI drafts when a thread moves on (Settings, AI drafts, on by default). Turn it off to leave all AI drafts as they are. See Settings.
  • Sent Items are indexed first. On the first run (and after a rebuild), Clippy now indexes Sent Items before the Inbox, so your writing-style skill is built early and drafts sound like you sooner, without waiting for the whole Inbox.
  • Latest Opus by default. AI drafts use the model opus (the newest Opus). This arrived in v0.0.9, below.
  • Clearer summaries. The AI drafts line in Activity now also counts drafts that were updated, moved to Deleted Items or kept.
  • Docs. The manual has new pages: Settings lists every setting with its default, and Activity lists the messages you can see there. The Tray menu page now covers every item.
  • Index upgrade. Clippy upgrades the index database to remember its own drafts. If you go back to an older version, it reports that the index is too new, and you rebuild it from the tray.

items.title: v0.0.9
items.text:
2026-11-15

  • AI drafts use the latest Opus. The default model is now opus, which always means the newest Opus model. If you never changed the model, Clippy switches you over. A model you typed yourself stays as it is. Effort stays medium.
  • With an API key, Clippy looks up the newest model of that family once a day and falls back to a known one if the lookup fails. Check shows which model opus means.
  • Your writing-style skill is visible. If Clippy can't read your my-email-style skill, Activity and the log say so once, and again when it's back.

items.title: v0.0.8
items.text:
2026-11-14

  • Clippy never sends anything now. send_meeting_invite and its confirmation dialog are gone. The new tool create_meeting_draft saves the meeting unsent in your calendar. You add the Zoom or Teams link and send it in Outlook. See Meeting drafts and create_meeting_draft.
  • Meeting drafts get the orange category Clippy draft invite. Clippy removes it once you have sent the meeting. Other categories stay.
  • With reply_to_id, Claude also leaves a highlighted note in a reply draft in Drafts, so you don't forget to send the invite.
  • New tray item Draft invites (n) lists your meeting drafts. Click one to open it in Outlook.
  • New yellow attention badge in the top-right corner of the tray icon, with the number of draft invites. The tooltip says what needs your attention.
  • Settings, Scheduling: Meeting invites is now Draft only or Disabled. The Send mode and the confirmation timeout are removed, and a saved Send loads as Draft only. The amber tray icon is gone.
  • The writing-style skill's meeting section tells Claude Code to call create_meeting_draft when you pick one of the offered times. Unedited skills get it automatically at the next start.

items.title: v0.0.7
items.text:
2026-11-14

  • Meeting times: find_free_times now ranks its suggestions by your calendar (times next to your meetings first, then next to tentative ones) and returns offers of exactly the meeting length plus a ready-to-paste offer_text, one option per line. New offer_cet option adds the time in CET and puts European office hours first, with the others under "Outside European office hours:".
  • AI drafts offer meeting times: when an email asks for a meeting, the draft gets options from your calendar, computed by Clippy, not by the model. Two new settings, Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting and Number of times to offer. See Meeting times.
  • The writing-style skill has a new section, "Offering meeting times", so Claude Code offers times the same way. Unedited skills get it automatically at the next start.
  • New tool email_stats: counts mail by sender, domain, recipient, folder, month, week, weekday or hour in one call. Counts and names only.
  • New tool query_index: one read-only SELECT over the views mail, mail_fts and mail_attachments, with full-text search and snippets. See Tools reference and Security.
  • AI drafts: an email Claude isn't confident enough about now shows a line in the Activity window with how to draft it anyway, and the pass summary counts "low confidence" separately.
  • Privacy fix: the log no longer contains the text of tool error messages, which could quote search text or SQL back. Only the kind of error is logged.

items.title: v0.0.6
items.text:
2026-11-13

  • Auto-update: the installed copy checks GitHub once a week and installs a newer full release at its next start. The download is checked against the release's SHA-256 and rolled back if the new version doesn't start. Set Settings, General, Updates to Install automatically (default), Only tell me or Don't check. See Updates.
  • New About Clippy's Revenge… window in the tray menu: version, update status, Check for updates, Update now and links to the documentation and release notes.
  • New balloons for a newer version, a finished update and a rollback.

items.title: v0.0.5
items.text:
2026-11-13

  • AI drafts: Clippy can draft replies to new mail in your writing style with Claude Code or an Anthropic API key. Off by default, asks for consent, saves drafts only, never sends, and the model gets no tools. See AI drafts.
  • Writing-style skill built from your own sent mail, saved as my-email-style in your Claude Code skills folder. Your edits are never overwritten automatically.
  • New tray submenu AI drafts and a Settings tab with the same name.

items.title: v0.0.2
items.text:
Released as a full (latest) release, so the installer and releases/latest links pick it up.

  • The installer and the README use the releases/latest download.
  • One-line install: paste irm ... | iex into PowerShell.
  • install.ps1 -WhatIf downloads and verifies the release without installing.
  • Never deletes email: this is now a documented hard rule, checked by a test that scans the source.
  • Reconcile refuses mass deletes from the index when Outlook's ids don't match the index.

items.title: v0.0.1
items.text:
First release.

  • Tray app with a local MCP server on 127.0.0.1, protected by a bearer token.
  • Local SQLite full-text index of your mailbox and shared mailboxes.
  • Tools: search_emails, get_message, get_attachment, save_attachments, create_draft, reply_draft, list_events, find_free_times, send_meeting_invite and index_status.
  • Tray menu, Settings and Activity windows, and a confirmation dialog for meeting invites.
  • install.ps1 installer and uninstaller.

items.title: Connect Claude Code
items.text: Clippy's Revenge serves MCP over streamable HTTP at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. The default port is 8765. Every request needs a bearer token that the app creates on first run. The server only listens on your own PC (127.0.0.1); see Security.

items.title: Add the server
items.text:
1. Right-click the paperclip in the system tray.
  2. Choose Copy "claude mcp add" command. A balloon says "Copied — paste it in WSL".
  3. Paste it into a terminal where Claude Code runs (Windows or WSL).

The command looks like this:

claude mcp add --scope user --transport http clippy http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Then start Claude Code and run /mcp to check that clippy is connected.

Tip

Settings, Connection has the same command, a Test connection button and the token. The command box hides the token until you press Show; Copy command always copies the full command.

The command contains your token, so treat it like a password. Don't paste it into chats, tickets or shared notes.

items.title: The port
items.text: The default is 8765. You can change it in Settings, Connection to any number from 1024 to 65535. Clippy asks before it applies the change, because Claude Code must then be set up again with the new command. If the new port can't be opened (another program uses it), the server stays on the old port, nothing is saved, and the Port field says Port <new> is in use or can't be opened. The server stays on port <old>.

items.title: The token
items.text:
The token is a random 32-byte value in hex. It is stored encrypted for your Windows user and never written to settings.json or to the log.

  • Copy auth token in the tray menu copies it.
  • Regenerate auth token… in the tray menu (or Regenerate… in Settings, Connection) creates a new one. The old token stops working at once, so run the new claude mcp add command again. Clippy asks you to confirm first, and Cancel is the default. In the Settings window the new token is applied when you press OK or Apply.

If you add the server again under the same name, remove the old entry first with claude mcp remove clippy.

items.title: From WSL
items.text:
In WSL2's default NAT mode, WSL cannot reach the Windows host's 127.0.0.1. Use mirrored networking (Windows 11 22H2 or later). In %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig on Windows:

[wsl2]
networkingMode=mirrored

Then run this in Windows and reopen your WSL shell:

wsl --shutdown

Check from WSL:

curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp     # expect: 401 Unauthorized

A 401 means the server is reachable and wants a token. Then paste the claude mcp add command in WSL.

The app listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It does not bind to the WSL virtual adapter, and it has no dependency on WSL interop: WSL talks to it over TCP. The same snippet is shown in Settings, Connection.

Files go to Windows folders

Attachments saved with get_attachment or save_attachments land in a Windows folder (by default %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge). From WSL you reach it as /mnt/c/Users/<you>/Downloads/Clippy's Revenge. To get an attachment straight into the folder where Claude Code works in WSL, use attachment_link and set CLIPPY_TOKEN as below.

items.title: Set CLIPPY_TOKEN for downloads
items.text:
The claude mcp add command stores your token in Claude Code's own config, but the shell where Claude Code runs commands doesn't have it. An attachment download link is fetched by that shell with curl, and it needs your token as well as the link. So you put the token in the shell's environment once:

  1. Open Settings, Connection. Next to From WSL there is a line that reads export CLIPPY_TOKEN=••••••••. The token is masked until you press Show next to the auth token.
  2. Press Copy WSL token line. This copies the full line, export CLIPPY_TOKEN=<your token>, to the clipboard, even while the line on screen is masked.

  3. In WSL, add the line to the end of ~/.bashrc, then reload it:

    echo 'export CLIPPY_TOKEN=<paste the token here>' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

    Or open ~/.bashrc in an editor and paste the copied line.

Check it from WSL. This should print the length of your token (64 characters) and not 0:

echo -n "$CLIPPY_TOKEN" | wc -c

To test the endpoint itself, ask Claude Code for an attachment (see attachment_link), or try an unknown link, which must answer 404 once the token is accepted and 401 when it isn't:

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPPY_TOKEN" \
  http://127.0.0.1:8765/files/0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000
# 404 = token accepted, no such link.  401 = token missing or wrong.

Use your own port instead of 8765 if you changed it.

After Regenerate auth token, update the export as well, exactly like the claude mcp add command: copy the line again, replace the old one in ~/.bashrc and run source ~/.bashrc (or open a new shell). Changing the port needs no change to CLIPPY_TOKEN; the link Claude gets always names the current port.

Treat the line like a password

~/.bashrc now holds your token. It is the same secret that is already in Claude Code's config, and it only works on your own PC (127.0.0.1). Don't paste the line into chats or tickets.

items.title: Check that it works
items.text:
In Claude Code, try:

Use the clippy index_status tool and tell me how many emails are indexed.

Right after install the index is still filling. Recent mail becomes searchable first, and Sent Items are indexed before the Inbox. See Indexing and search.

All the tools Claude can then use are in the Tools reference.

items.title: Test connection
items.text:
Settings, Connection, Test connection sends two requests to the running server: one without the token (it must answer 401) and one with it (it must answer as the clippy MCP server). It tests the running server, not changes you haven't applied yet. The result is one of:

Message What to do ✓ Connection works: 127.0.0.1:<port> needs the token and answers MCP. Nothing. ✗ The server isn't running. Check the tray icon for the reason. Look at the tray icon and the Activity window. A port that is in use shows as an error. ✗ Nothing answers on 127.0.0.1:<port>. The server isn't listening there. Check the port number. ✗ The server on 127.0.0.1:<port> didn't answer within 5 s. Wait a moment and try again. ✗ The server answered without a token (HTTP <code>). Another program may be using port <port>. Change the port. ✗ The server rejected the token (HTTP 401). Restart Clippy. If it persists, regenerate the token. ✗ The server answered HTTP <code> to initialize. The server has a problem, or another program holds the port. Check the Activity window, then restart Clippy or change the port. ✗ The server answered, but not with an MCP initialize result. Another program holds the port. Change the port. ✗ Another MCP server (<name>) is answering on port <port>. Another program holds the port. Change the port.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• /mcp shows clippy as failed, or Claude gets 401. The token in Claude Code is old (you regenerated it) or was cut when pasting. Run Copy "claude mcp add" command again and add the server again.
  • Connection refused. Clippy isn't running (check the tray), or the port differs from the one in the command.
  • From WSL nothing connects. WSL is probably in NAT mode. Use mirrored networking as above and run the curl check.
  • Tools work but searches find nothing. The index is still filling. Ask Claude to call index_status.
  • A browser can't call it. On purpose: any request that carries an Origin header is refused, so web pages can't reach the server.

More help is in Troubleshooting.

items.title: Does it work with the new Outlook?
items.text: No. It needs classic Outlook, because it drives Outlook through COM. The new Outlook has no COM interface.

items.title: Does it work with IMAP or POP accounts?
items.text: Not supported. An Exchange or Microsoft 365 mailbox is required.

items.title: Can it send email?
items.text: No. Clippy never sends anything, neither mail nor meetings, with or without AI. It has no send function at all, and the code is checked for this on every build. It saves drafts and you send them from Outlook. Meeting invites are saved unsent in your calendar too. See Meeting drafts and Security.

items.title: Why can't Clippy send a meeting invite?
items.text: Outlook's object model can't add a Teams or Zoom link, and you would add one by hand anyway. So Clippy saves the meeting unsent, marks it with the orange category Clippy draft invite, and lists it under Draft invites in the tray. You open it, add the link and send it. Clippy then removes its category.

items.title: What is the yellow number on the tray icon?
items.text: The attention badge. It counts meeting drafts waiting for you to add a link and send them. It disappears when you have sent them all.

items.title: Can it delete or move my mail?
items.text: No. It never deletes email, never empties Deleted Items and never moves your mail. There is one narrow exception, and it only concerns Clippy's own drafts: see the next question. Removing rows from Clippy's own search index is not touching mail.

items.title: Why did a draft go to Deleted Items?
items.text: Only an AI draft that Clippy wrote itself can go there. When a newer message arrives in the same thread, Clippy re-checks its earlier draft. If no reply is needed any more, or a better one was written, Clippy moves the old draft to Deleted Items (from where you can drag it back). It does this only when you haven't edited it, opened it or sent it, and the Activity window records it. Nothing is ever deleted for good. You can turn it off with Update or remove my AI drafts when a thread moves on in Settings, AI drafts. See Outdated drafts.

items.title: What does "Rescan emails from the last 24 hours" do?
items.text: It is in the tray, under AI drafts. It goes through the last day of mail, oldest first, drafts replies where one is needed and re-checks Clippy's own drafts in those threads. It asks first, showing how many Claude calls it may use, and stops at your daily limit. Click Cancel rescan to stop it. It works even when automatic drafting is off. See Rescan and the tray menu.

items.title: Why isn't my writing style used yet?
items.text: The first writing-style skill is built from your Sent Items. Clippy indexes Sent Items before the Inbox and builds the skill as soon as they are done, so you don't have to wait for the whole first backfill. Until then, drafts have no personal style. See Your writing style.

items.title: Which Claude model does it use?
items.text: By default the latest Opus: the model setting is opus, which always means the newest Opus. You can type sonnet or haiku the same way, or a full model name. See Settings.

items.title: Where can I see what Clippy did?
items.text: In the Activity window: double-click the tray icon. It lists syncs, tool calls, drafts and updates for the current session, without mail text.

items.title: Why do reply subjects start with "Re::"?
items.text: It is intentional. Reply drafts always start with Re:: (double colon).

items.title: Can it write replies for me?
items.text: Yes, if you turn on AI drafts. Clippy then asks Claude to draft replies to new mail in your style and saves them in Drafts. It never sends them. It is off by default and asks for your consent first.

items.title: Will the AI draft offer meeting times?
items.text: Yes, when an email asks for a meeting and Offer meeting times when an email asks for a meeting is on (the default). Clippy picks the times from your calendar itself, the model never sees them, and each option is its own line that you can delete. For senders in Europe it adds the time in CET. See Meeting times.

items.title: Why does a meeting time say CET in summer?
items.text: The label is always "CET" for Central European time, also while Europe is on summer time. The time itself uses the real offset (+02:00 in summer), so the number is right.

items.title: Why did a draft come out without a CET time for a sender in Europe?
items.text: Clippy guesses where the sender is from the Date header and the address ending, and can miss, for example for a .com address in winter UK time. See Senders in Europe. You can add or delete the CET part by hand.

items.title: An email got no draft and the Activity window says "low confidence". What now?
items.text: Claude wasn't sure enough that a reply was needed, below your Minimum confidence. Such an email is decided once and not retried. To get a draft anyway, select the email in Outlook and use Draft a reply to the selected email in the tray menu. See Emails Clippy decides not to draft.

items.title: Does AI drafting send my mail to Anthropic?
items.text: Yes, while it is on: the email being answered, thread excerpts, up to 5 related earlier emails, attachment names, the extracted text of attachments and of synced shared files (unless you turn that off), your facts file and your style guide go to Claude through your own Claude Code (or your API key). Once a week, with the writing-style update, samples of your sent mail go too, and up to 20 pairs of an AI draft and what you sent after editing it (unless you turn that off). Files themselves and images never do. See what is sent.

items.title: Does Clippy learn from how I edit its drafts?
items.text: Yes, since version 0.1.1, unless you turn it off. When you send a reply that began as an AI draft, Clippy notes what you changed. It keeps a redacted copy of the draft and of what you sent in its local index (at most 1,500 characters each, the newest 20 edited pairs, deleted after 30 to 90 days). Nothing leaves your PC then. At the next writing-style update (weekly, or Regenerate), if there are at least 3 pairs, up to 20 are sent to Claude, which adds an "Edits I usually make to drafts" section to your style. Drafts that used attachment text are never kept. Untick Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts in Settings, AI drafts, to stop it. See Learning from how you edit drafts.

items.title: How do I make Clippy forget how I edited its drafts?
items.text: Turn off Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts in Settings, AI drafts: nothing more is recorded or sent. That doesn't erase what is already stored; it ages out within 90 days. To erase it now, use Rebuild index… in the tray and choose My mailbox or All mailboxes (it deletes the index file that holds the records). Then press Regenerate in Settings to write a style without the "Edits I usually make to drafts" section.

items.title: Why does Activity say "noted how you edited 3 sent drafts"?
items.text: Clippy looked at your recently sent mail, found replies that started as its AI drafts and compared them with the drafts. It says how many it noted, including drafts you sent unchanged. See Activity.

items.title: Does Clippy read my attachments?
items.text: For AI drafts, yes, since v0.1.1 and unless you turn it off. It reads the text of PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, HTML and .eml attachments (and attached emails) of the email and its thread, and of OneDrive/SharePoint files linked in them that are synced to your PC, and sends that text to Claude for that one draft. It is never stored or indexed. Images are not read. See Attachments and shared files, and Settings to turn it off.

items.title: Why couldn't Clippy read my shared file?
items.text:
When Clippy can't read a file from a link or cloud attachment, the draft starts with a yellow note, for example Clippy: Couldn't read the shared file Plan.docx (not synced to this PC). The reasons:

  • Not synced to this PC. Clippy never downloads from the network. It reads only the copy that your OneDrive sync client already keeps on this PC. The file must be in your OneDrive, a synced SharePoint or Teams library or folder, or a folder you added with Add shortcut to My files. Sync the library (in SharePoint, Sync) or add the shortcut, then rescan or draft the reply again. "Specific people" and other secret-token sharing links, Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=… links, and 1drv.ms and onedrive.live.com links can't be matched to a local file even when it is synced.
  • Not from your organization. The note says Clippy only opens shared files from people in your organization. Clippy opens a shared link only when the email came from you or from your own email domain (or a subdomain), so that outsiders can't make it put a file from your OneDrive into a draft. If your own address is at a free or consumer mail provider such as outlook.com, hotmail.com, gmail.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com or GMX, only links you sent yourself (or the shared mailbox's own address) are read. Links are taken only from the text each person wrote: links in quoted replies or forwarded mail are ignored. Attached files are read whoever sent them.
  • Not a OneDrive or SharePoint link. Dropbox, Google Drive and other links are never opened. There is no note for these.
  • The file is too slow. An online-only file is downloaded by OneDrive when Clippy opens it. If that takes longer than 10 seconds (or the draft's 20 seconds), the note says it took too long. While one PDF that took too long is still being processed, other PDFs are skipped with the same note until it finishes.
  • The file itself. password-protected, larger than 25 MB, no text in it, maybe a scan (Clippy has no OCR), the file seems damaged, or Clippy can't read .<ext> files for formats such as .doc, .xls, .rtf and .zip.
  • The setting is off. If Read attachments and synced shared files for drafts is unticked, no files are read and there are no notes.

Notes are shown only for files of the email itself and for earlier files the email mentions by name. More about the notes, with their exact texts, is in The yellow notes.

items.title: Where does Clippy keep the attachment text?
items.text: Nowhere. It is read into memory for one draft request and then dropped. The next draft in the same thread reads the file again. Outlook attachments pass through a private folder, %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ai-files\, for a moment and are deleted at once (and at start-up, if one was left). See Security.

items.title: What is the "Today: … tokens" line?
items.text: A tally of today's Claude calls and the tokens they used, shown while AI drafts consent exists: at the top of the tray's AI drafts menu and in the Activity window. For example Today: 18 AI calls, ~210k tokens (in 190k / out 20k). It counts drafts, re-checks, rescans and style updates, not calls that never started. Only counts are stored (30 days). See Token tally.

items.title: How do I stop drafts for one sender?
items.text: Select an email from them in Outlook and use Don't draft for this sender (or …this sender's domain…) in the tray's AI drafts menu. To undo, delete the line in Settings, AI drafts, Never draft for. See Don't draft for this sender.

items.title: Does Clippy work in a non-English Outlook?
items.text:
Yes. Since v0.1.1 Clippy recognizes the Drafts and Deleted Items folders by their role, so they are skipped for related mail and earlier attachments whatever Outlook calls them. A folder indexed before v0.1.1 under its translated name keeps its old entries until you add the folder again or use Rebuild index…. See Drafts and Deleted Items in other languages.

To cut quoted history from mail, Clippy recognizes the reply headers Outlook writes in English, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Italian, Swedish, Polish and Japanese (for example From:/Von:/Från:/差出人: blocks and "On … wrote:" lines). In other languages more of the quoted text may reach Claude as part of an email.

items.title: Can I tell the AI drafts my Zoom link or how I like to sign off?
items.text: Yes. Use Edit my facts… in the tray, under AI drafts. It opens a file with headings for your role, links, office hours, standard answers, people and How I want replies written. Whatever you write there is used in every draft, and your reply preferences win over the writing style. See Facts about you.

items.title: Does Claude see my older emails too?
items.text: A few. With Include related earlier emails on (the default), each draft request carries up to 5 earlier emails from the same mailbox that match the topic or the sender, including your own replies to that person, so the draft fits the history. You can turn it off in Settings, AI drafts. See Related earlier mail.

items.title: What is the yellow line at the top of an AI draft?
items.text: The reason line: one sentence starting Clippy: that says why the draft was written. Delete it before you send. Deleting it counts as editing the draft, so Clippy won't replace or move that draft later. You can turn the line off in Settings, AI drafts. See The reason line.

items.title: Does Clippy sign in to Claude or read my Claude login?
items.text: No. You sign in to Claude Code yourself in a terminal, and Clippy only asks it whether you are signed in. It never reads Claude Code's stored credentials.

items.title: Why didn't a mail get a draft?
items.text: It may have arrived before you turned AI drafts on, be older than the age limit, be a newsletter or automatic mail, match a never-draft rule, or not need a reply. See Rules.

items.title: Is the writing-style file safe?
items.text: It is a Claude Code skill in %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-style, so your interactive Claude Code sessions can load it. Review, edit or delete it any time. See the security note.

items.title: Does my mail go to the cloud?
items.text: Clippy has no cloud component. It runs on your PC and listens on 127.0.0.1. What Claude Code then sends to its model is the text of the mail it reads, so treat that as you would any use of an AI assistant with your mail. The optional AI drafts feature also sends mail to Claude, with your consent.

items.title: Do I need an app registration or admin consent?
items.text: No. There is no Graph API, Entra app registration or OAuth. If Outlook can open the mail, Clippy can use it.

items.title: Can Claude answer "who emails me the most?" or "how much mail do I get per month?"
items.text: Yes, in one call. Ask in plain language, for example "top 10 people who emailed me in the last year, with counts" or "mail per month since January". Claude uses email_stats, which counts mail in the local index by sender, sender domain, recipient, folder, month, week, weekday or hour. It returns counts and names, never mail text, and works while Outlook is closed.

items.title: Can Claude run its own searches with SQL?
items.text: Yes, with query_index: one read-only SELECT over three views of the index, including full-text search with snippets. Nothing can be changed and nothing outside those views can be read. See Security.

items.title: Does Outlook have to be running?
items.text: For indexing, yes. Clippy never starts Outlook on its own. Searching the existing index works while Outlook is closed. Tools that read live from Outlook (full messages not yet indexed, attachments, drafts, calendar) need it running.

items.title: Can Claude Code in WSL use it?
items.text: Yes, with WSL's mirrored networking. See Connect Claude Code.

items.title: Can other computers or web pages reach it?
items.text: No. It binds to 127.0.0.1 only, requires a token, and rejects any request that has an Origin header.

items.title: How far back does search go?
items.text: 12 months by default. Change it in Settings, Index (1 to 120 months).

items.title: Are attachments searchable?
items.text: Attachment file names are searchable. Their contents are never indexed. To read an attachment, Claude saves it with get_attachment (or, from WSL, fetches it with attachment_link) and reads the file.

items.title: Where does it save attachments?
items.text: %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge by default. Claude can only save to allowed folders, which you control in Settings, General.

items.title: Where do downloaded files go when Claude uses a download link?
items.text: Into the folder where Claude Code ran the curl command, for example your WSL project folder. With attachment_link, Clippy makes a one-time link and the shell downloads the file itself. Clippy keeps a private copy in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\links\ only until the download ends or 10 minutes pass, then deletes it. That folder is normally empty.

items.title: How do I get an attachment into WSL?
items.text: Ask Claude Code to fetch it. It uses attachment_link and runs the curl command it gets back. You need CLIPPY_TOKEN set in WSL once: see Set CLIPPY_TOKEN.

items.title: curl says 401 when Claude downloads an attachment
items.text: The shell doesn't have your token, or has an old one. Open Settings, Connection, press Copy WSL token line and put the line in ~/.bashrc in WSL, then source ~/.bashrc. After Regenerate auth token you must do this again. A 401 does not use up the link, so the same command works once the token is right (if the 10 minutes haven't passed).

items.title: curl says 404 when Claude downloads an attachment
items.text: The link is single use and lasts 10 minutes. A 404 means it was already used, has expired, was never made, or Clippy was restarted (which clears all links). Ask Claude for a new link. The link names the port it was made on, so after a port change old links no longer work either.

items.title: Can I download the same link twice?
items.text: No. Each link works once. Ask Claude for a new one.

items.title: Why does Claude say the attachment is too big for a link?
items.text: Links handle files up to 100 MB, with at most 10 open links, 200 MB open in total and 20 links per 10 minutes. For a bigger file, Claude uses get_attachment to save it on the Windows side. See the limits.

items.title: Can I use a shared mailbox?
items.text: Yes. Check it under tray, Shared mailboxes. See Shared mailboxes.

items.title: Does it start with Windows?
items.text: Yes by default. Turn it off with the Start with Windows item in the tray menu.

items.title: How do I update?
items.text: By default Clippy checks GitHub once a week and installs a newer version at its next start. To update at once, open About Clippy's Revenge… in the tray and press Update now, or run the install one-liner again. See Updates and Install.

items.title: How do I turn updates off?
items.text: Settings, General, Updates: choose Don't check (no automatic checks) or Only tell me (a balloon, no download). See Updates.

items.title: Does Clippy send anything to GitHub?
items.text: Only the weekly update check and the download, as plain requests that carry just the version number. No mail, no settings, no telemetry. See what is sent.

items.title: How do I uninstall?
items.text: See Uninstall.

items.title: Why does SmartScreen warn me?
items.text: The exe is not code-signed yet. The installer verifies its checksum.

items.title: Where are the logs?
items.text: %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs. Use the tray's Open log folder.

items.title: How it works
items.text:
Clippy keeps a local SQLite database with full-text search (FTS5) of your mail. Claude's searches run against this database, so they are fast and still work while Outlook is busy. Full messages and attachments are fetched live from Outlook when needed.

Indexing needs Outlook to be running. Clippy attaches to a running Outlook and never starts it (only the tray's Start Outlook item does, when you click it). If Outlook isn't running, indexing waits and the tray icon turns grey with a !.

What is indexed: subject, body, sender, recipients (To and CC), dates, folder, read state, the conversation topic and the attachment file names, sizes and whether they are inline. Attachment contents are never indexed, and no file is ever stored in the index. A very long email is stored cut at 2,000,000 characters.

Indexing only reads. It never changes, moves or deletes your mail.

items.title: First run: backfill
items.text:
On the first run, Clippy reads your mail from the retention cutoff up to now, newest first, so recent mail becomes searchable first. The tray icon is blue and animated.

Folder order: Sent Items first. In each mailbox the folders are processed in this order: Sent Items (and its subfolders), then Inbox, then every other folder you chose. Each folder is finished before the next one starts. So on a first run you see the Sent Items backfill complete before the Inbox backfill begins. The reason: AI drafts learn your writing style from your sent mail, so Clippy builds the style file as soon as Sent Items are indexed, while the Inbox is still being read. The order is the same in every cycle; only the first run makes it visible.

What you see while it runs:

Where Text Tray tooltip Clippy — indexing Inbox 1,240 / 8,000 (2025-11 → now). For a shared mailbox the name is added, for example indexing helpdesk@… Inbox 300 / 2,000 Activity, start of a folder Sent: backfill started, 3,200 emails to index (2025-11 → now) Activity, end of a folder Sent: backfill complete Activity, each cycle with changes Inbox +12, Sent +3 (1.8 s) Activity, purge removed 310 emails older than 2025-11-12 Tray tooltip, new mail Clippy — pulling new mail (Inbox +12) Tray tooltip, purge Clippy — removing mail older than 12 months Tray tooltip, when done Clippy — idle · 48,210 emails · synced 2 min ago Tray tooltip, paused Clippy — indexing paused

Sent Items is shown as Sent. The progress bar in the Activity window is only shown during a backfill. If you quit in the middle, the backfill resumes where it stopped.

Ask Claude to use index_status to see whether the backfill is complete.

An older index may run one quiet extra pass after an update that adds conversation data to existing rows. It shows as Updating thread data and reads no mail bodies.

items.title: What is indexed
items.text:
Setting Default Where Retention 12 months (1 to 120) Settings, Index Folders Inbox and Sent Items Settings, Index Sync interval 5 minutes (30 s to 1 h) Settings, Index

All settings are listed in the Settings reference.

Retention. Raising it starts a new backfill for the older mail. Lowering it removes older mail from the index right away. This only affects Clippy's index, never your mailbox.

Folders. Pick any folders in the Settings tree. Subfolders are separate entries, and a search for folder="inbox" does not include subfolders. Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts and Deleted Items always mean that mailbox's default folder, whatever language Outlook uses: a German Gesendete Elemente is indexed and shown as Sent Items, and Entwürfe as Drafts. Other folders keep their own names, such as Archive\2025 or Inbox\Projects.

items.title: Keeping up to date
items.text:
Every sync interval (and when you click Sync now), Clippy picks up new and changed mail, then removes mail past the retention cutoff from its index. The interval counts from the end of the last cycle, and the first cycle runs at start-up.

Once a day for each folder, a reconcile pass compares the index with Outlook. It adds missing mail, refreshes read/unread state, and removes index rows for mail that is gone from Outlook. Reconcile only touches the index. As a safety measure, when it would remove 20 or more rows it removes none if Outlook listed nothing for the folder, if none of Outlook's ids match the index, or if those rows are more than half of the folder's indexed mail. Activity shows a line such as Reconciled Inbox: 3 removed, 1 added, 12 read-state updated.

items.title: Pause, sync now and rebuild
items.text:
• Pause indexing stops the current cycle at the next batch. Batches that are finished are kept. Sync now is ignored while paused; Resume indexing starts a cycle at once. The paused state is not saved: Clippy starts unpaused.
  • Sync now runs a cycle immediately.
  • Rebuild index… (tray menu, or the Rebuild button in Settings, Index) asks for confirmation, then deletes the index database for your mailbox or for all mailboxes and starts again from scratch. Search finds less until it finishes. Use it if results look wrong. It never changes your mail. After a rebuild the folder order above applies again: Sent Items first.

items.title: Purge and retention
items.text:
After each cycle, mail older than the retention cutoff is removed from the index. The Purging state shows only when there is something to remove. When more than 10% of the rows go at once, the database file is compacted. Nothing in Outlook is touched.

Clippy's own records about AI drafts (which emails it decided on, and so on) are kept for 30 days. They hold no mail text. See Security.

items.title: Shared mailboxes
items.text:
Exchange mailboxes mounted in your Outlook profile (shared or additional mailboxes) appear under the tray menu Shared mailboxes.

  • Check one to start indexing it into its own database file.
  • Uncheck one to stop. You choose Delete its index, Keep index file or Cancel. The mailbox is disabled either way.
  • Each shared mailbox can have its own folders and retention in Settings, Index. Its Sent Items are also indexed before its Inbox. Because mailboxes run one after the other (yours first), a shared mailbox's Sent Items come after the last folder of your own mailbox.
  • If Outlook isn't running, the list shows only configured mailboxes.
  • A shared mailbox that isn't mounted, or a folder that doesn't exist, is skipped with one error line in Activity.

Tools use a shared mailbox with mailbox="<the shared mailbox's address>", or search all enabled ones with mailbox="all". AI drafts for a shared mailbox are a separate opt-in; see AI drafts.

items.title: Search tips
items.text:
You rarely write queries yourself, but these are what Claude can use in query:

Query Meaning budget report Both words (AND) budget OR forecast Either word "annual review" The exact phrase proj* Words starting with proj

Search is not case-sensitive and ignores accents. Characters such as -, + or : are treated as plain text, so budget-2026 or C++ never cause an error. Only an uppercase OR works as an operator.

Filters such as sender, subject, date_from and attachment_ext narrow the results. See the search_emails reference. For counts and custom questions, see email_stats and query_index.

items.title: Where the index lives
items.text:
One database per mailbox in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\: index.db for your mailbox and index-<address>.db for each shared mailbox, plus the -wal and -shm files next to them. It holds message bodies as plain text, like Outlook's own cache file. See index at rest.

The database has a schema version. If a newer version of Clippy changed it, the database is upgraded when the app starts. An older Clippy refuses a newer database and does not touch it; use Rebuild index… after a downgrade.

Settings, Index shows live numbers for the selected mailbox: number of emails, oldest and newest mail, database size and last sync.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Windows 11 with classic Outlook (not the new Outlook), signed in.
  • An Exchange or Microsoft 365 mailbox. IMAP/POP-only profiles are not supported.
  • No administrator rights are needed.

items.title: Install or update
items.text:
Paste this into PowerShell:

irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

The script downloads the latest release, checks ClippysRevenge.exe against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt, installs it and starts it. Run the same line again to update.

Clippy also updates itself once a week by default, so you only need the line above to install, to update at once, or to repair a broken install. To change how Clippy updates, see Settings, General, Updates.

It installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ClippysRevenge\, adds a Start menu shortcut called "Clippy's Revenge", and starts the app. A paperclip appears in the system tray. The app is set to start with Windows (you can turn that off in the tray menu or in Settings).

The first start reads your mail from Outlook in the background: Sent Items first, then the Inbox, newest mail first within each folder. You can search the newest mail while it runs. See Indexing.

SmartScreen

The exe is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen warns the first time it runs. Choose More info, then Run anyway. The installer verifies the SHA-256 checksum of the download before it installs anything.

items.title: Preview first with -WhatIf
items.text:
-WhatIf downloads and verifies the release but changes nothing on your PC:

& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1))) -WhatIf

items.title: Install from a file
items.text:
Download install.ps1 from the latest release and run it:

.\install.ps1                                # same as the one-liner
.\install.ps1 -Source .\ClippysRevenge.exe   # install a local build instead
.\install.ps1 -NoStart                       # install but don't launch

You can also download ClippysRevenge.exe from the release and run it directly.

Option Meaning -Source <path> Install a local ClippysRevenge.exe instead of downloading -NoStart Don't start the app after installing -WhatIf Show what would happen; on the download path, download and verify only -Uninstall Remove the app (see below) -Purge With -Uninstall: also delete settings, token, index and logs, without asking

items.title: Uninstall
items.text:
& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1))) -Uninstall

This stops the app and removes the exe, the Start menu shortcut and the "Start with Windows" entry. It then asks whether to delete your settings, token, index and logs. Add -Purge to delete them without asking. If you answer no, they stay on disk.

items.title: What gets stored where
items.text:
What Where Program %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ClippysRevenge\ClippysRevenge.exe Settings, token and API key (encrypted) %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ Index, logs and update state %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ Short-lived files: an attachment waiting for its download link (links\, deleted after the download or when the link expires) and an attachment being read for an AI draft (ai-files\, deleted right after reading) %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ Saved attachments %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge

Your writing-style skill for AI drafts is stored under %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-style, and your facts file under %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-context. The uninstaller removes neither.

items.title: Next step
items.text: Connect Claude Code.

items.title: Security model
items.text: Clippy's Revenge gives an AI tool access to your mail, so it is built to do as little as possible and to keep that access on your PC.

items.title: What it never does
items.text:
• Never sends anything. Not mail and not meetings. Clippy has no send call at all. Mail drafts are only saved, and a meeting draft is saved unsent in your calendar. You send both from Outlook. A test scans the source to make sure it stays that way.

  • Never deletes email. Clippy never calls delete, permanent delete or "empty Deleted Items", and never moves existing mail. There are exactly two narrow exceptions, both about Clippy's own drafts:

    1. a reply draft Clippy has just created is moved into Drafts;
    2. an outdated AI draft of Clippy's own is moved into Deleted Items (not deleted, so you can still recover it). This happens only when the draft carries Clippy's AI marker, is unchanged since Clippy saved it, is unsent, is still in Drafts, is not open in a window, and you haven't replied in the thread. The checks run again right before the move. See Outdated drafts.

    Nothing is ever permanently deleted and Deleted Items is never emptied. Retention and reconcile remove rows from Clippy's own index only, never from your mailbox. A test scans the source to make sure it stays that way. - Never starts Outlook on its own. It attaches to a running Outlook. The tray's Start Outlook item, which you click yourself, is the only exception. - Never uses the cloud. No Microsoft Graph, no Entra app registrations, no OAuth. Nothing leaves your PC except what Claude Code sends to its model, update checks to GitHub, and, while AI drafts are on, what Clippy sends to Anthropic (see Outbound connections). - Never indexes or stores attachment contents. Only file names are indexed. For AI drafts, the text of attachments and of synced OneDrive/SharePoint files is read in memory for one draft request, sent to Claude, and never written to the index, settings, logs or Activity. - Never touches your Claude credentials. AI drafts run your own signed-in Claude Code, or an API key you type in. Clippy never reads Claude Code's stored sign-in.

items.title: Network
items.text:
• Localhost only. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 and nothing else. Other computers on your network can't reach it. It does not bind to the WSL virtual adapter either, which is why WSL needs mirrored networking.
  • Bearer token. Every request must carry Authorization: Bearer <token>. The comparison is constant-time. Requests without a valid token get an empty 401.
  • Token storage. The token is stored encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your Windows user, in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\token.bin. It is never written to settings.json or to logs. Regenerate it any time from the tray. If you save an Anthropic API key for AI drafts, it is stored the same way (DPAPI-encrypted) in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\anthropic-key.bin; the file exists only if you save a key.
  • Browsers are blocked. Any request with an Origin header gets a 401, so a web page can't call the server, even from your own PC.
  • No OAuth prompts. The 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate header, so MCP clients don't start an OAuth flow.

items.title: Attachment download links
items.text:
The attachment_link tool lets a shell, usually Claude Code in WSL, download one attachment as a file. It adds one endpoint, GET /files/<link token>, on the same server. Everything in Network applies to it unchanged: loopback only, constant-time bearer check, no browsers.

  • Two secrets are needed. The request must carry your bearer token and the link token. The link appears in the Claude Code conversation, so a leaked link alone is useless. Anything else on your PC that can reach 127.0.0.1 (another Windows user, other WSL processes) can't use it without the bearer token either. The token reaches the shell through CLIPPY_TOKEN, set once by you (see Connect). It is never put in a tool result.
  • Link token. 32 random bytes, 43 characters (A-Z a-z 0-9 - _). It is kept in memory only, never written to disk, never shown in Activity and never logged.
  • One download, 10 minutes. The link is removed before the first byte is sent. A second request gets 404. A request that fails the bearer check (401) never reaches the link, so it doesn't use it up. After 10 minutes the link is gone.
  • Private folder. Clippy saves the attachment into %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\links\ when the link is made. The folder is created for your Windows user only: no inherited permissions, full control for your user account alone. Files there are named with 32 random hex characters and .bin, never the attachment's name. If the folder is a junction or symlink, or its permissions can't be set, attachment_link refuses.
  • No copies left behind. The file is deleted right after its download ends (completed or interrupted), when the link expires (checked every 60 seconds), when the app exits, when the port changes or the server restarts, and at app start, when any leftover <32 hex>.bin file in that folder is removed. A file that can't be deleted is retried at the next check. Other files in the folder are left alone.
  • Limits. 100 MiB per attachment, 10 open links, 200 MiB open in total and 20 links per rolling 10 minutes. See the limits.
  • Nothing is indexed. Attachment content never enters the index, and the link code doesn't touch the index at all. A test checks this.
  • No path from the model. The model chooses an email and an attachment, never a path. The file path is made by Clippy from a random name inside its own folder.
  • GET only. Other methods on /files/... answer 405 with an empty body. HEAD isn't served. A Range header is ignored: the whole file is always sent, so a partial request can't use the link up.
  • Unknown, expired or used links answer 404 with an empty body and no detail. The same goes for a token that isn't 43 characters of the allowed letters, and for a link whose file has gone missing. 401 (no or wrong bearer token, or an Origin header) has an empty body too.
  • Safe download headers. Content-Type: application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition: attachment with a cleaned file name, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Cache-Control: no-store.
  • Logs. The link token is in the URL, so the web server's own request logging is held to Warning level, and any /files/<token> that still reaches a log is masked as /files/[redacted]. Clippy's own lines name only outcomes and sizes, never the token, the path or the file name.
  • Activity. A download shows as attachment download or attachment download failed, with no file name. See Activity.

Clippy still never sends anything, never deletes or moves mail and never touches Outlook items for this: it only saves a copy of the attachment, like get_attachment, and deletes its own copy.

items.title: Outbound connections
items.text:
Clippy makes exactly two kinds of outbound connection:

  • GitHub, for updates. Once a week (unless you set Don't check), the installed copy asks GitHub for the latest release and may download ClippysRevenge.exe and SHA256SUMS.txt. These are plain unauthenticated requests that send only a ClippysRevenge/<version> user agent. Nothing about you, your mail, the index or your settings is sent, and there is no telemetry. See Updates.
  • Anthropic, only while AI drafts are on. See AI drafts data flow.

All connections use HTTPS with normal certificate checks. Update downloads follow redirects only to GitHub's own hosts.

items.title: Update trust model
items.text:
An update is accepted when it comes over HTTPS from the project's GitHub release and its SHA-256 matches the SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release. This proves the file is the one published in the release and arrived intact. It does not prove who published it: whoever can publish a release in the repository (a stolen account or token, a compromised workflow) could publish a matching exe, and copies set to Install automatically would install it within a week without asking. Clippy starts only its own installed exe after an update, never runs a script, and rolls back a version that doesn't start.

If you want to review each release first, set Settings, General, Updates to Only tell me or Don't check. See Updates.

items.title: File access
items.text:
Every file path a tool reads or writes goes through a path policy. A path must be inside an allowed folder:

  • the attachment folder, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\Clippy's Revenge by default, which is always allowed
  • %USERPROFILE%\Documents, which is in the list by default (you can remove it)
  • any folders you add in Settings, General

Relative paths, .. that leads out of an allowed folder, UNC and device paths (\\server\..., \\?\...), alternate data streams, reserved device names and paths through a junction or symbolic link are refused. This stops a prompt-injected email from making Claude write into places like the Startup folder, or read files such as ~/.ssh. A refused path is shown as Blocked in the Activity window.

When a meeting draft has been sent, Clippy changes one thing on it: it removes its own Clippy draft invite category. It stores only the meeting's Outlook id in draft-invites.json, not its subject, times or attendees.

items.title: Index at rest
items.text:
The index holds message bodies as plain text, like Outlook's own cache (OST) file. It is protected by your Windows profile's file permissions and by your disk encryption. There is no extra encryption layer.

Turn on BitLocker

Without full-disk encryption, anyone with your disk can read the index.
