items.title: AI drafts data flow
items.text:
AI drafts are the one feature that sends mail text off your PC. They are off by default and need your consent. While on, Clippy sends to Anthropic (through your Claude Code or your API key):

  • the email being answered, with its quoted history (cut at 20,000 characters)
  • up to 8 earlier messages of the same thread from the local index, own text only (quotes and signatures cut), each cut at 4,000 characters
  • up to 5 related earlier emails from the same mailbox, your own text only, at most 4,000 characters in all (see Related earlier mail); you can turn this off with Include related earlier emails
  • the text of your facts file, without comments, when you filled it in. Don't put passwords or other secrets in it
  • attachment file names, and, while Read attachments and synced shared files for drafts is on, the text of the attachments of the email and its thread and of OneDrive/SharePoint files they link to that are already synced to your PC (at most 40,000 characters per draft). See Attachment text
  • your name and address, today's date, and your writing-style guide
  • once a week, up to 200 samples of your sent mail from the last 12 months for the style guide, each cut at 1,500 characters, with addresses, links and phone numbers removed
  • with that weekly style update (or Regenerate), up to 20 pairs of an AI draft and the reply you sent after editing it, redacted and cut to 1,500 characters each, when at least 3 exist and Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts is on. See Learning from your edits
  • when Clippy re-checks an outdated draft, the text of its own earlier draft (cut at 4,000 characters) and the newer messages of the thread

Never sent: images, any file itself (only extracted text), other mail or folders from the index, your calendar, mail from shared mailboxes you haven't turned on, your Claude credentials, and your API key (except to Anthropic as the key itself).

The model gets no tools: it can't read files, search mail or run anything. Its answer is validated and cleaned to plain formatting and saved as a reply draft, never sent. Claude Code (or the API) and your Claude plan terms govern what happens to the data after it leaves Clippy.

Clippy never reads Claude Code's stored credentials, never calls an API with them, and never offers a claude.ai sign-in. It runs your own claude command, or uses an API key you typed in (stored DPAPI-encrypted). Logs and the Activity window don't contain mail text, prompts, your facts, related mail, the style guide, the reason line or Claude's answers.

items.title: Attachment text and shared files
items.text:
What Clippy does and doesn't do when it reads files for a draft (details):

  • In memory only. The text lives while one request is built and sent. It is never written to the index, settings, logs or Activity, and there is no cache. Logs and Activity hold counts only, never file names, links, paths or text.
  • Private temp folder. To read an Outlook attachment, Clippy saves it as <random>.bin (or .msg for an attached email) in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ai-files\, a folder only your Windows user can use. It reads the bytes and deletes the copy at once. At app start every leftover is deleted. If the folder is a junction or symlink, or its permissions can't be set, attachments aren't read. The attachment's own name never reaches a path.
  • Nothing in Outlook changes. Clippy opens attached emails read-only, closes them without saving, and never sends, moves or deletes anything.
  • Files are parsed, not run. Text is extracted by Clippy's own code. Macros, embedded objects, linked content and fields are never read or followed. Zip-based Office files are checked for too many entries, a huge size or a suspicious compression ratio before reading. Each file is capped at 25 MB, 20,000 characters and 10 seconds.
  • Shared links never leave your PC. Only links to Microsoft's OneDrive/SharePoint hosts are considered (*.sharepoint.com, onedrive.live.com, d.docs.live.net, 1drv.ms, after unwrapping Safe Links). Every other link is not touched at all. Clippy makes no network request for a link, uses no Microsoft Graph and no sign-in, and reads only the copy your own OneDrive client has synced to this PC. If the file is online-only, opening it makes your OneDrive client download it. Paths are checked like all file access, so a shortcut or junction can't lead out of the synced folder.
  • Only from your organization. Links and cloud attachments are opened only when the email was sent by you, by the shared mailbox's own address, or by an address in your own domain (or a subdomain of it), so a stranger can't make Clippy put a file from your OneDrive into a draft for them. A free or consumer mail provider is not an organization: with such an address only links you sent yourself count. Clippy knows about 40 of them, such as outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com, gmail.com, yahoo.com, icloud.com, aol.com, Proton, GMX, web.de, t-online.de, mail.ru, qq.com, comcast.net and fastmail.com, plus country versions such as hotmail.co.uk or yahoo.fr. Links are read only from the text each person wrote, never from quoted replies, forwarded mail or lines that start with >.
  • Prompt injection. The model is told that file text is data, never instructions, and it still has no tools. The worst a malicious file can do is produce a bad draft.
  • Off switch. Untick Read attachments and synced shared files for drafts and none of this happens.

items.title: Learning from your edits
items.text:
What Clippy does and doesn't do with your edited drafts (details):

  • Stored locally, redacted. When Clippy saves an AI draft it keeps the reply text (without the reason line, notes and signature) in your own mailbox's index, with addresses, links and phone numbers replaced and cut to 1,500 characters. A draft that used attachment text is not kept, so file text never reaches this store.
  • Matched from the index only. Clippy compares the draft with your sent reply using mail it has already indexed. It makes no Outlook call for this and never changes or moves the sent mail.
  • Small and purged. Texts are kept for the newest 20 edited pairs only; unmatched draft texts expire after 30 days; the remaining numbers go after 90 days. No tool, including query_index, can read these records, and they are deleted with the index (Rebuild index…).
  • Never logged. Logs and Activity hold counts and exception type names only.
  • Leaves the PC once a week at most. Only the writing-style update sends pairs (up to 20, redacted) to Claude, as data it is told never to follow. The model still has no tools.
  • Off switch. Untick Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts: nothing new is recorded or matched and no pairs are sent. Existing records age out or go with Rebuild index….
  • The result is part of your style skill. The "Edits I usually make to drafts" section Claude writes lives in the same Claude Code skill file as the rest of the guide, with the same warning below. It is told to include no names, addresses, links or numbers.

The facts file is visible to Claude Code

The facts file is also a user-level Claude Code skill, %USERPROFILE%.claude\skills\my-email-context\SKILL.md, so your interactive Claude Code sessions (which have tools) can load it. Keep secrets out of it. Delete the folder if you don't want that. See Facts about you.

The style skill is visible to Claude Code

The style guide is saved as %USERPROFILE%.claude\skills\my-email-style\SKILL.md, a user-level Claude Code skill, so your interactive Claude Code sessions (which have tools) can load it. Review it with View in Settings, edit it, or delete it any time. See Your writing style.

items.title: Statistics and SQL queries
items.text:
email_stats and query_index let Claude count and query the local index. They expose the same data that search_emails and get_message already return, and nothing else: no sync state, settings, AI decisions or internal ids, and no attachment content (only file names are indexed). email_stats returns counts and names, never mail text.

query_index is read-only through several independent layers, so that a mistaken or malicious query can't change anything:

  • The connection to the index file is opened read-only, with writing switched off.
  • Only three views (mail, mail_fts, mail_attachments) can be read. Every table, column and function access is checked, and anything else is refused, such as other tables, PRAGMA, ATTACH, loading extensions and every write.
  • One SELECT per call, no ? parameters, a 10 second limit, at most 1000 rows, and long text is cut at 2,000 characters.
  • The views are created for that one call and leave the index file unchanged.

It can't touch your mailbox in Outlook at all: it only reads Clippy's own index.

The text of a query (SQL), the values it returns and SQLite's error messages are never written to the log. See Logs.

items.title: Prompt injection
items.text: Email is untrusted text, and Claude reads it. Clippy limits what a malicious email could make Claude do: it can't send mail, can't delete mail, can only write files to allowed folders, and every meeting stays unsent until you send it yourself. AI drafts get a model with no tools at all, so the worst a malicious email can do there is produce a bad draft. Still, check drafts before you send them, and read a meeting draft before you click Send.

items.title: Logs
items.text: Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs and kept for 7 days. They contain tool names, counts and errors. The token, the saved API key and any sk-ant-… or Bearer … text are masked, as is the token in an attachment /files/<token> link, and mail bodies and search text are not logged. Activity events show subjects and counts only. The SQL of a query_index call and the text of a tool's error message (which can quote a search or a SQL error back to Claude) are not logged either, only the kind of error. Tool calls appear as the tool name, with counts and timings.

items.title: Unsigned executable
items.text: The release exe is not code-signed yet. The installer and the automatic updater check its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt from the same release before installing. That proves integrity, not the publisher. See Update trust model.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Open Settings from the tray menu, Settings…. The window is titled Clippy's Revenge — Settings and has five tabs: Connection, Index, Scheduling, General and AI drafts.

  • Changes apply when you press OK or Apply. Cancel discards them. The exceptions are on the AI drafts tab: giving consent and saving or removing an API key take effect at once.
  • A wrong value is rejected, with the reason next to the field (for example Must be between 1024 and 65535. or Must be a whole number.). Pressing OK or Apply then switches to the tab with the first problem.
  • After Apply the line at the bottom says Saved., or names a side effect that failed (for example Couldn't update the Windows startup entry: <reason>).
  • Everything is saved in %APPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\settings.json, except the auth token (token.bin) and an Anthropic API key (anthropic-key.bin). Both files are next to settings.json and are encrypted for your Windows user (DPAPI).
  • Before a port change takes effect, the window asks first, because Claude Code must be set up again. The same goes for regenerating the token.
  • If you start the app a second time, the running copy opens Settings (on the Connection tab, or brings an open Settings window to the front).
  • Where a setting is "live", it applies at once, without a restart.

The tables list each setting's name in settings.json. You don't need to edit the file: see Only in settings.json.

items.title: Only in settings.json
items.text:
One setting has no box in the window: AiDrafting.TimeoutSeconds (default 180, 30 to 900), the time limit of one drafting call. Change it in settings.json while Clippy is not running; Clippy rewrites the file whenever a setting changes.

The file accepts // comments and trailing commas. If it isn't valid JSON or a value is out of range, Clippy keeps it as settings.json.bad, starts with defaults and notes this in the log.

Some values are internal. Leave them alone:

  • AiDrafting.ConsentedAtUtc and AiDrafting.EnabledAtUtc: when you gave consent and when you last turned automatic drafting on.
  • AiDrafting.RelatedMailNoticeShown, AiDrafting.AttachmentsNoticeShown and AiDrafting.EditsNoticeShown: the one-time notices about related mail, attachments and learning from edits were shown.

items.title: Tools reference
items.text:
Clippy's Revenge gives Claude Code thirteen tools. You normally don't call them yourself: you ask Claude in plain language and it picks the right tool. This page lists every tool and its parameters, which is useful when you want to know what Claude can and can't do.

Tool What it does search_emails Search the local index get_message Read one email in full get_attachment Save one attachment to disk save_attachments Save attachments of all emails matching a search attachment_link Make a one-time download link for one attachment, for WSL or another shell create_draft Save a new email draft reply_draft Save a reply draft list_events List calendar events find_free_times Suggest meeting times from free/busy create_meeting_draft Save a meeting unsent in your calendar. Nothing is sent index_status Show index and sync state email_stats Count mail by sender, domain, folder or time query_index Run one read-only SELECT over the index

There is no send_meeting_invite tool. Older versions had one; it was replaced by create_meeting_draft, which never sends.

items.title: What the tools can and can't do
items.text:
• Nothing is ever sent. Clippy has no send function. Mail tools only save drafts in your Drafts folder, and the meeting tool only saves a meeting unsent in your calendar. You review and send both in Outlook.
  • Nothing is deleted. No tool deletes or moves your mail. The only mail Clippy ever moves is an outdated AI draft of its own, and that is not a tool: see Outdated drafts.
  • Read-only tools. search_emails, get_message, index_status, email_stats, query_index, list_events and find_free_times change nothing. get_attachment and save_attachments write files to disk, only inside the allowed folders. attachment_link also creates a file, but only a short-lived private copy for a download link. create_draft, reply_draft and create_meeting_draft create items in Outlook.
  • Which tools need Outlook running. search_emails, email_stats, query_index and index_status use the local index and work while Outlook is busy or closed. get_message falls back to Outlook for mail that isn't indexed. Attachments, drafts, list_events, find_free_times and create_meeting_draft always need Outlook.

items.title: Common conventions
items.text:
• mailbox: empty means your own mailbox. An SMTP address means that shared mailbox, which must be enabled in the tray. Search tools (search_emails, email_stats, query_index, save_attachments) also accept all. Tools that take an id find the mailbox from the id.
  • Dates: ISO date (2026-03-01) or date-time (2026-03-01T14:30), in local time. A space may replace the T, seconds are optional, and a date-time ending in Z, +hh:mm or -hh:mm is honored. A date-only end date includes the whole day.
  • Numbers out of range: limit, offset, top, max_rows, days_ahead and max_suggestions are moved into their range without an error. days (list_events), duration_minutes, earliest_hour and latest_hour give an error instead.
  • Recipients: "Last, First <address>; other-address". Separate people with ;, never ,, because names are often written "Last, First".
  • File paths: every path must be inside an allowed folder. See file access. Relative paths resolve under the attachment folder (see Settings). A refused path returns an error that names the allowed folders, and is recorded in Activity.
  • Errors: tools return a message that tells Claude what to fix. The most common ones are in Errors Claude may see.

items.title: search_emails
items.text:
Searches the local index. It is fast and works while Outlook is busy. All filters are optional and combine with AND. Results are newest first. Only synced mail is indexed; use index_status to check coverage.

Parameter Type Description query string Free text over subject, body, sender, recipients and attachment file names. Words are ANDed. Use OR between words for alternatives, "quotes" for a phrase, and a trailing * for a prefix. sender string Substring of the sender's name or email address recipient string Substring of To or CC. Also accepts a list like Name <address>; other-address, which matches mail involving any of them subject string Substring of the subject date_from string Earliest date, inclusive date_to string Latest date, inclusive folder string inbox, sent (or sent items), or another indexed folder path such as Inbox\Projects (not case-sensitive, / works as well as \). Subfolders are not included. Empty means all folders has_attachment bool true: only mail with real (non-inline) attachments; false: only mail without attachment_name string Substring of any attachment file name (inline images included) attachment_ext string Exact attachment extension, with or without the dot (pdf or .pdf) unread bool true: only unread; false: only read mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all limit int Maximum results, 1 to 200 (default 50) offset int Results to skip, for paging (default 0)

The text filters (sender, recipient, subject, attachment_name) ignore upper and lower case. A blank text filter means no filter. A recipient that contains ; or < is read as a list of people (up to 50 of them are used). Outlook's default folders keep their English names in the index (Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, Deleted Items), also when Outlook shows them in another language.

Each result has id, mailbox, folder, date (local time), from, sender_email, to, subject, has_attachments, attachments[] (position, filename, size, inline) and snippet. With query, the snippet shows the matching words between **; otherwise it is the start of the body. Pass a result's id to get_message to read the body.

Errors: a date that can't be read gives date_from "<text>" is not a valid date. Use an ISO date like 2026-03-01 or a date-time like 2026-03-01T14:30 (local time).

Example request

"Find unread mail from accounting with a PDF attached since 1 March."

Claude calls search_emails with sender="accounting", unread=true, attachment_ext="pdf", date_from="2026-03-01".

items.title: get_message
items.text:
Returns one email in full: headers, complete body and attachment list. It reads the index first. If the email isn't indexed yet, it reads it live from Outlook, which needs Outlook to be running.

Parameter Type Description id string, required The id of an email, as returned by search_emails

The result has id, mailbox, folder, date, from, sender_email, to, cc, subject, unread, has_attachments, attachments[], internet_message_id, body and source (index or outlook). A very long email is stored cut at 2,000,000 characters and ends with the line [Clippy indexed only the first 2,000,000 characters of this email.]. If Outlook has to be asked and isn't running, the error is Outlook is not running. Ask the user to start Outlook (tray → Start Outlook) and try again.

items.title: index_status
items.text:
Shows the state of the local index: per-mailbox counts, oldest and newest indexed mail, last sync and whether the first backfill is complete. It also says whether Outlook is running and what Clippy is doing right now. Use it to explain why a search found nothing, or to check indexing progress.

Parameter Type Description mailbox string Optional shared mailbox address. Empty means all configured mailboxes

The result has state (what Clippy is doing: Idle, Serving, Drafting, Paused, Purging, Syncing, Backfilling, OutlookUnavailable or Error), progress (text such as Inbox (2025-11 → now) 1240/8000, or null when there is nothing to report), outlook_running (true, false, or null before the first attempt) and mailboxes[]. Each mailbox has mailbox, total_emails, folders (count per folder), oldest, newest, db_size_bytes, last_sync and backfill_complete.

items.title: email_stats
items.text:
Counts emails in the local index, grouped, in one call. Use it for questions such as "top 10 people who emailed me last year" or "how much mail do I get per month". It returns counts and names only, never mail text. It is read-only and fast, because the counting runs inside the index.

All the filters of search_emails work here (query, sender, recipient, subject, date_from, date_to, folder, has_attachment, attachment_name, attachment_ext, unread, mailbox), with the same meaning. There is no limit or offset.

Parameter Type Description group_by string, required What to group by. See the table below top int Number of groups to return, 1 to 200 (default 10) order string count: largest groups first (default). key: by key, chronological for month, week and hour, Mon to Sun for weekday include_cc bool For recipient and recipient_domain: also count CC addresses (default true) mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all

group_by values

Value Key sender The sender's email address, lower case. name is the display name in the newest email of the group sender_domain The part of the sender address after the @ recipient Each To address, plus each CC address when include_cc is true. An address counts once per email. name is the display name seen in the newest email recipient_domain The same, by domain. A domain counts once per email folder The folder path month yyyy-MM week ISO week, yyyy-Www weekday Mon to Sun hour 00 to 23

month, week, weekday and hour use your Windows time zone. (unknown) is the group for senders with no valid address. Recipients with no valid address are skipped, so recipient and recipient_domain have no (unknown) group. Any other group_by value returns an error that lists the valid ones.

The result is group_by, mailbox, total (matching emails, not recipient entries), distinct (number of groups), truncated (true when there are more groups than top) and rows. Each row has key, count, first and last (the dates of the oldest and newest email in the group, local time with offset), and name for sender and recipient.

With mailbox="all", the counts of every enabled mailbox are added together by key. An email that is in two mailboxes counts twice.

Example requests

"Who emailed me most in the last year? Top 10 with counts."

Claude calls email_stats with group_by="sender", folder="inbox", date_from one year ago.

"How much mail do I get per month?" is group_by="month", order="key". "Who do I write to most?" is group_by="recipient", folder="sent". "Which companies send me the most mail?" is group_by="sender_domain".

For joins, snippets or any other question that grouping can't answer, use query_index.

items.title: query_index
items.text:
Runs one read-only SQLite SELECT over the local email index. Use it for questions the other tools can't answer in one call: joins, custom grouping and full-text search with snippets. For plain counts, email_stats is simpler. It works while Outlook is busy or closed, and only synced mail is indexed.

Parameter Type Description sql string, required One SELECT (WITH and VALUES also work). Write values into the SQL; ? parameters are not supported mailbox string Empty, a shared mailbox address, or all max_rows int Maximum rows returned, 1 to 1000 (default 200)

Views. The query sees exactly these three views, which hold the same data that search_emails and get_message return.

View Columns mail id (the id that get_message takes), doc (join key), mailbox (empty for your own), folder, date (local time, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss), unix_time (UTC seconds), sender_name, sender_email, to_addrs, cc_addrs (Name <email>; ...), subject, topic (conversation topic), body (plain text), unread (0 or 1), has_attachments (0 or 1, not counting inline images), attachment_names (one file name per line) mail_fts The full-text index: mail_fts (use it with MATCH, snippet(), highlight()), rank, doc, subject, body, sender_name, sender_email, to_addrs, cc_addrs, attachment_names. Join to mail on doc mail_attachments doc, position, filename, size, is_inline (0 or 1). Only file names are indexed, never attachment content

For full-text search, filter with WHERE mail_fts MATCH '...' (FTS5 syntax: words are ANDed, OR, NOT, "a phrase", prefix*, column:word) and sort with ORDER BY rank (best first). snippet(mail_fts, n, ...) and highlight(mail_fts, n, ...) take a column number: 0 subject, 1 body, 2 sender name, 3 sender email, 4 To, 5 CC, 6 attachment names. bm25(mail_fts) also works.

Limits

  • One statement only. PRAGMA, ATTACH, every write and every other table are refused, with an error that names what was not allowed.
  • 10 seconds in total, at most 1000 rows (max_rows), at most 100 columns, long text cells cut at 2,000 characters, and about 1,000,000 characters of results in total. The SQL itself may be at most 20,000 characters. On a large mailbox add a LIMIT and a date or folder filter.
  • With mailbox="all" each mailbox is queried separately and the rows are joined with a leading mailbox column. Counts and other aggregates are therefore per mailbox; use email_stats for counts merged across mailboxes.

The result has columns, rows (numbers stay numbers, empty values are null), row_count, truncated, truncated_cells (how many cells were cut) and elapsed_ms. When it stops early it also gives truncated_reason: max_rows (the row limit was reached) or size (the next row would pass the total size limit).

Example queries

Top senders in your Inbox in the last year:

SELECT sender_email, count(*) AS n FROM mail
WHERE folder = 'Inbox' AND unix_time >= strftime('%s','now','-1 year')
GROUP BY sender_email ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 10

Mail per month:

SELECT substr(date,1,7) AS month, count(*) AS n FROM mail
GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

Full-text search with snippets:

SELECT m.id, m.date, m.subject,
       snippet(mail_fts, 1, '**', '**', '…', 12) AS hit
FROM mail_fts JOIN mail m ON m.doc = mail_fts.doc
WHERE mail_fts MATCH 'budget AND 2026' ORDER BY rank LIMIT 20

PDF attachments by sender:

SELECT m.sender_email, count(*) AS n
FROM mail_attachments a JOIN mail m ON m.doc = a.doc
WHERE lower(a.filename) LIKE '%.pdf' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 20

Read-only, by several layers

The query runs on a read-only connection to the index with writing switched off, and every table and column access is checked. Only the three views above can be read, not sync state, settings or anything else in the database. See Security.

The main query_index errors:

Situation Message (shortened) Empty sql sql is required: one SELECT over the views mail, mail_fts and mail_attachments. Over 20,000 characters sql is longer than 20,000 characters. Shorten the query. More than one statement query_index runs exactly one SELECT statement. Remove everything after the first statement. A write, PRAGMA, ATTACH, another table or column query_index only reads the views mail, mail_fts and mail_attachments with one SELECT. Not allowed here: <what>. ? parameters query_index takes no parameters; write the values into the SQL. More than 100 columns query_index returns at most 100 columns. Longer than 10 seconds The query ran longer than 10 seconds and was stopped. Add a date range, a folder or a LIMIT, or use email_stats for counts. Query needs too much memory The query needs too much memory. Simplify it: fewer nested WITH clauses, fewer or shorter computed columns. A value over 16 MB A value in the query is too large (more than 16 MB). SQL syntax or other SQLite error SQL error: <SQLite's message>. query_index reads the views ... Index not ready (not indexed yet, being rebuilt) The index for <mailbox> isn't available right now. Check index_status.

email_stats errors: group_by must be one of sender, sender_domain, recipient, recipient_domain, folder, month, week, weekday, hour. and order must be count or key.

items.title: Attachments
items.text: Attachments are saved with a live call to Outlook, so Outlook must be running. Files are never overwritten: a duplicate name becomes name (2).ext.

items.title: get_attachment
items.text:
Saves one attachment of an email to disk and returns its path, file name and size.

Parameter Type Description id string, required The id of an email, from search_emails filename string File name of the attachment (whole name, case-insensitive) position int 1-based position in the email's attachment list save_dir string Folder to save into. Empty means the attachment folder. Relative paths go under it. Must be inside an allowed folder

If you pass neither filename nor position, Clippy takes the only attachment, or the only real (non-inline) one when the rest are inline images. Otherwise the error lists the attachments (for example This email has 3 attachments. Pass filename or position to choose one: 1 "report.pdf", 2 "notes.docx", 3 "image001.png" (inline).) so Claude can choose; the list shows at most 20. If you pass both, they must agree. If two attachments have the same name, pass position. Inline attachments can be fetched by name or position. The returned filename is the attachment's original name; the saved file may be called name (2).ext, and characters Windows doesn't allow in file names become _.

An attached email that has no file name is listed as <subject>.msg (or (no name).msg); any other attachment without a name is listed as attachment-<n>. Names recorded in the index by older versions, without the .msg, still match in get_attachment, save_attachments and attachment_link.

items.title: save_attachments
items.text:
Finds emails with the same filters as search_emails and saves their attachments into one folder. attachment_name and attachment_ext also choose which attachments are saved. Inline images are skipped unless include_inline is true. Returns saved[], failed[], count (number saved) and a note when nothing matched or nothing was eligible. Each saved entry has id, mailbox, position, filename, path and size; each failed entry has id, mailbox, position, filename and error. One failure doesn't stop the rest, except when Outlook closes or stops responding: then every attachment not yet saved is listed in failed with that error. Emails are saved newest first. The note is No emails matched the filters. or <n> email(s) matched, but none had attachments to save. Inline attachments are skipped unless include_inline is true.

Parameter Type Description save_dir string Folder to save into. Empty means the attachment folder query, sender, recipient, subject, date_from, date_to, folder, has_attachment, attachment_name, attachment_ext, unread, mailbox Same as in search_emails include_inline bool true: also save inline attachments such as embedded images (default false) limit int Maximum number of emails, 1 to 200 (default 50) offset int Emails to skip, for paging

items.title: attachment_link
items.text:
Makes a one-time download link for one attachment of an email. Use it when Claude Code runs in WSL (or any other shell) and should get the attachment as a real file in its own working folder, without you copying it over from the Windows side.

Tool Where the file goes Result get_attachment A Windows folder inside the allowed folders A Windows path (C:\...) save_attachments One Windows folder, for many emails A list of Windows paths attachment_link The shell's current folder, through curl A link and a curl command

The file's bytes never pass through Claude: the tool returns only the link, and the shell downloads the file. Nothing about the attachment's content is indexed or put into the conversation. get_attachment is unchanged and stays the right tool when you want the file on the Windows side.

Setup needed once: the shell must have CLIPPY_TOKEN set, because the download needs your auth token as well as the link. See Set CLIPPY_TOKEN in WSL.

Parameter Type Description id string, required The id of an email, from search_emails filename string File name of the attachment (whole name, case-insensitive) position int 1-based position in the email's attachment list

Choosing the attachment works exactly as in get_attachment: with more than one attachment, pass filename or position; with neither, the error lists the attachments so Claude can choose; with both, they must agree; inline attachments can be fetched by name or position. There is no save_dir, because the file is not saved to a folder you choose.

Result:

Field Meaning url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/files/<link token>. The link token is 43 characters of letters, digits, - and _ filename The attachment's original name size Size in bytes of the copy Clippy made expires_at When the link stops working: 10 minutes after it was made, in your local time with the offset, for example 2026-11-15T14:35:00+01:00 curl The command to run in the shell (below) note One download only. If curl answers 401, CLIPPY_TOKEN isn't set in this shell: ask the user to copy the auth token from the Clippy tray menu and add export CLIPPY_TOKEN=<token> to ~/.bashrc.

The curl command has this shape:

curl -fsS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPPY_TOKEN" -o 'Q3 report.pdf' 'http://127.0.0.1:8765/files/<link token>'

The real token is never in the result: the shell fills in $CLIPPY_TOKEN itself. The file name in the command is made safe to put in single quotes: characters Windows doesn't allow in file names and every ' become _, and a leading - or . is replaced by _, so the name can never be taken for an option or be a hidden file. The file is saved with that name in the folder where the command runs, and an existing file with the same name is overwritten by curl, so ask Claude to run it in the folder you want.

How the link behaves:

  • One download only. The first successful request uses the link up. Running the same command again gives 404.
  • Expires after 10 minutes. After that the link is gone, even if never used.
  • Needs both tokens. The request must carry your bearer token ($CLIPPY_TOKEN) and the link token. A request without the bearer token gets 401 and does not use the link up.
  • Made at once. Clippy saves the attachment through Outlook when the link is made, not when it is downloaded. The download then works even if Outlook closes or gets busy, and Outlook problems show up as normal tool errors instead of a curl failure.
  • Gone after use. Clippy deletes its private copy right after the download (finished or interrupted), when the link expires, and when Clippy starts or exits. Changing the port or restarting the server also drops every open link, because the links name the old port. See Security.
  • The download is GET only (other methods get 405) and the whole file is always sent.

items.title: attachment_link limits
items.text:
Expired links don't count. A link whose download is still running counts until the download ends.

Limit Refusal text 100 MiB per attachment The attachment is <n> MB; attachment_link handles up to 100 MB. Use get_attachment to save it on the Windows side. (<n> is the size rounded up) At most 10 open links Too many open download links (10). Download them or wait until they expire (10 minutes), then try again. At most 200 MiB of open links in total The open download links already hold 200 MB. Download them or wait until they expire, then try again. At most 20 links per rolling 10 minutes Too many download links in the last 10 minutes (20). Try again in <n> min. (<n> is whole minutes, at least 1)

Before Clippy asks Outlook for anything, it checks the number of open links, the open bytes (refused when they already reach 200 MiB) and the rate, in that order. The size limit is checked when Outlook reports the attachment's size, and again on the saved copy. When the copy is registered, all four are checked once more (size first); a link that would push the open total over 200 MiB is refused then, and the copy is deleted.

Other errors:

Situation What the message says No id id is required. Use the id from search_emails. Outlook isn't running, busy, or the email is gone The same messages as in Errors Claude may see Several attachments and none chosen, or a name that doesn't match The attachment list, as for get_attachment The private folder can't be used Clippy can't use its private download folder. Use get_attachment instead. The server is restarting Clippy's server isn't running, so it can't make a download link. Try again in a moment. Example request

"Get the PDF attached to the email about the Q3 numbers into this folder."

Claude finds the email with search_emails, then calls attachment_link with its id and filename="Q3 report.pdf". It gets back size: 482113, an expires_at ten minutes from now and the curl command above. In WSL, Claude runs the command and Q3 report.pdf appears in the current folder. If you ask it to run the same command again, curl fails with 404, because the link was single use. Ask for a new link instead.

items.title: Drafts
items.text: Drafts are only ever saved to the Drafts folder. You review and send them from Outlook. Nothing is sent by these tools. Drafts made by these tools carry a hidden marker that says Clippy's tools created them (AI drafts have their own marker, see AI drafts).

items.title: create_draft
items.text:
Creates a new draft. The default signature is added below the text when you have one set. Every attachment path is checked before anything is created; if one is refused, nothing is created, and the error ends with Nothing was created. Checks run in this order: mailbox (all is refused), recipients (to needs at least one), attachments. Line breaks in the subject become spaces.

Parameter Type Description to string, required Recipients, separated by ; subject string, required Subject line body string, required Plain text, or an HTML fragment when html is true cc string Same format as to bcc string Same format as to html bool true when body is HTML (default false) attachments string[] Paths to existing files in allowed folders. Relative paths resolve under the attachment folder mailbox string Empty means your own mailbox, or an enabled shared mailbox. The draft goes to that mailbox's Drafts folder and is sent on its behalf

Returns id, subject, mailbox (empty for your own) and signature_added.

Example request

"Draft an email to my manager asking for the Q3 numbers."

Claude calls create_draft with to set to your manager's address, subject="Q3 numbers" and a body. The draft appears in Drafts. You edit and send it yourself.

items.title: reply_draft
items.text:
Creates a reply draft to an email. The body is placed above the quoted original, followed by your reply signature when one is set.

Subjects start with Re::

Reply subjects start with Re:: (a double colon). This is intentional.

Parameter Type Description id string, required Id of the email to reply to, from search_emails body string, required Plain text reply, or an HTML fragment when html is true reply_all bool true: reply to all recipients (default false) html bool true when body is HTML (default false) mailbox string Empty means the mailbox the original is in, or an enabled shared mailbox

Returns id, subject, mailbox and signature_added. mailbox defaults to the mailbox the original email is in.

items.title: Calendar
items.text: See Calendar and meetings for how these fit together.

items.title: list_events
items.text:
Lists calendar events in a time window, with recurring events expanded into instances. Sorted by start, at most 500. Defaults to the next 7 days.

Parameter Type Description start string Window start. Default: today 00:00 end string Window end. A date-only end covers that whole day. Default: start plus days days int Window length in days when end isn't given, 1 to 366 (default 7). Outside that range: days must be between 1 and 366. mailbox string An enabled shared mailbox's calendar. Empty means yours

The result has the resolved start and end of the window, count, truncated (true when the 500 limit was reached) and events[]. Each event has id, subject, start, end, all_day, location, organizer, is_recurring and busy_status (free, tentative, busy, out_of_office or working_elsewhere). An end that isn't after start gives end must be after start.

items.title: find_free_times
items.text:
Finds times when everyone is free, from Outlook free/busy. Nothing is booked. Returns numbered suggestions (whole free blocks) with start, end, adjacent and a ready-to-show text, and offers: options of exactly duration_minutes, with offer_text ready to paste into an email. People whose free/busy can't be read (for example, people outside your organization) are listed in unknown_attendees and ignored.

Ranking. Times right before or after one of your meetings come first (within 15 minutes, on the same day), then times next to a tentative meeting, then everything else, each group in date order. adjacent says which: busy, tentative or none. Free/busy can't tell a meeting from other busy time, so "next to a meeting" means "next to busy time". Without your own calendar (include_me=false, or your free/busy can't be read), every time is none. Whether tentative time blocks a slot follows Tentative counts as busy in Settings, and the zone label (PT below) follows Time-zone label.

Offers. offers and offer_text hold at most max_suggestions options of exactly duration_minutes, in the same ranking, one per line. Options are taken in 30-minute steps from the start of each free block (plus one that ends exactly at its end) and never overlap each other:

1. Tue 11/18  10:00–11:00 PT  (19:00–20:00 CET)
2. Wed 11/19  14:00–15:00 PT  (23:00–00:00 CET)

With offer_cet=true (for someone in Europe) each line also shows the time in Central European time, always labelled CET, also in summer. Options between 08:00 and 18:00 CET come first. If there are fewer than wanted, the rest follow in a second list headed Outside European office hours:, numbered on from the first. Each offer has list: main or outside_hours. If your PC is already on Central European time, there is no CET part and no second list. See Meeting times in AI drafts.

Parameter Type Description recipients string, required Attendees as Name <email>; Name <email>. At most 50. May be empty when include_me is true duration_minutes int Minimum free block length, and the exact length of each offer, 1 to 1440 (default 60) days_ahead int Calendar days to search, counted from the day of date_from, 1 to 60 (default 10) date_from string Start date or date-time. Default: now earliest_hour int Working-hours start, 0 to 23. Default: from Settings latest_hour int Working-hours end, 1 to 24, later than earliest_hour. Default: from Settings business_days_only bool Skip Saturdays and Sundays. Default: from Settings include_me bool Also check the calendar owner (default true) max_suggestions int 1 to 20 (default 5). Also the most offers returned mailbox string Empty means your calendar, or an enabled shared mailbox offer_cet bool true when the person you are writing to is in Europe: offers also show CET, Europe office hours first (default false)

The result has suggestions[] (n, label, start, end, adjacent), text, offers[] (n, label, start, end, adjacent, list), offer_text, unknown_attendees[] and attendees[] (the people whose free/busy was read, with name and email). start and end are local times with offset, for example 2026-10-15T13:00:00-07:00. With no suggestions, text says why: no readable free/busy, or no free block in the days searched. The server remembers nothing between calls, so to book option N, Claude passes that option's start and end to create_meeting_draft.

If offer_cet is true but the PC has no Central European time zone, the offers have no CET part, and a warning is written to the log once.

Example request

"Find an hour next week for me and the two people on this email. One of them is in Berlin."

Claude calls find_free_times with recipients set to their two addresses, duration_minutes=60, date_from set to next Monday and offer_cet=true, then pastes offer_text into the email it drafts.

items.title: create_meeting_draft
items.text:
Saves a meeting in your calendar without sending it. Clippy never sends anything. You add the Zoom or Teams link in Outlook and send the invite yourself. See Meeting drafts for the whole workflow.

The meeting gets the category Clippy draft invite, is listed in the tray under Draft invites, and counts toward the tray icon's badge. If the invite answers an email, pass reply_to_id and a note is saved in Drafts.

Every recipient must resolve in Outlook, or nothing is created. In Disabled mode (see Settings, Scheduling) the tool refuses with Meeting drafts are disabled in Clippy's Revenge. Ask the user to enable them in the tray settings (Meeting invites: Draft only), then try again. Clippy checks the arguments first, then reply_to_id, then the recipients, and only then creates and saves the meeting. With mailbox, you need delegate or editor rights on that mailbox's calendar, or the tool refuses. Each call adds one line to Activity, such as meeting draft saved for 2 attendees: Thu 10/15 10:00–11:00, or meeting draft not created: <reason> when it fails. The body never appears there.

Parameter Type Description recipients string, required Attendees as Name <email>; Name <email> or bare emails, separated by ; subject string, required Meeting subject start string, required Local start date-time, e.g. 2026-03-01T14:30. A date without a time is not accepted. An offset is converted to local time end string, required Local end date-time, after start and in the future body string Plain-text invite body location string Location, for example a room mailbox string An enabled shared mailbox to save the meeting in. Empty means yours reply_to_id string The id of the email that asked for the meeting (from search_emails). Saves a note in Drafts as a reply to it. An unknown id is an error and nothing is created

To book option N of a find_free_times result, or of times offered in a draft, pass that option's start and end.

No Teams or Zoom link

Outlook's object model has no supported call to add a Teams or Zoom link. The result always tells Claude that the meeting has none and that you add it in Outlook. The old teams argument is gone.

The result has:

Field Meaning status Always saved_as_draft message For Claude: the meeting was saved without sending, it has no Teams or Zoom link, and it is listed in the tray under Draft invites. With a note, it adds A note was saved in Drafts as a reply to the email. subject, start, end What was saved. Times are in the same format as find_free_times mailbox, organizer, recipients Whose calendar it is in, who organizes it and who is invited category Clippy draft invite, or null if the category couldn't be set (the meeting is still saved) note_draft_id Only with reply_to_id: the id of the note draft note_error Only if the note failed: the meeting is saved, but the note in Drafts couldn't be created

Example

Claude calls create_meeting_draft with recipients set to the sender's address, subject="Project sync", start="2026-10-15T10:00", end="2026-10-15T11:00" and reply_to_id set to the id of the sender's email. The meeting appears unsent in your calendar, a note reply appears in Drafts, and the tray shows Draft invites (1).

items.title: Errors Claude may see
items.text:
Every tool error is a plain sentence that tells Claude what to do next. Common ones:

Situation What the message says Outlook isn't running Outlook is not running. Ask the user to start Outlook (tray → Start Outlook) and try again. Outlook is busy Outlook isn't responding. It may be busy, offline or showing a dialog box. Ask the user to check Outlook, then try again. If this call was creating a draft or a meeting, check Outlook for it before retrying. Index can't be opened The email index could not be opened; see the tray (Error state). Restart Clippy or use Rebuild index. Unknown or disabled mailbox Mailbox "<input>" is not configured or not enabled. Available mailboxes: <list>. To use another shared mailbox, ask the user to enable it in the Clippy tray menu under Shared mailboxes. Mailbox enabled but not in your Outlook profile Mailbox "<address>" is configured but is not open in Outlook. Ask the user to add it to their Outlook profile, then try again. mailbox="all" on a tool that doesn't support it Mailbox "all" only works with search tools. Use one mailbox: <list>. (create_draft and reply_draft word the second sentence a little differently) Unknown email id Email "<id>" was not found in Outlook. It may have been deleted or moved to a folder that isn't indexed. Run search_emails again to get a current id. attachment_link refused One of the limit messages Path outside the allowed folders Path '<path>' is not allowed: <reason>. Allowed folders: <list>. See file access Meeting drafts turned off See create_meeting_draft

Tool errors are not written to the log with their text, because they can quote what was searched for.

items.title: Tray menu
items.text: Clippy's Revenge has no main window. Everything lives in the paperclip icon in the system tray (you may need to click the ^ to see hidden icons). This page covers the icon, the right-click menu and the balloons. The other windows have their own pages: Settings and Activity.

items.text:

items.title: Attention badge
items.text:

The tooltip then ends with · 1 draft invite needs your attention (or · 3 draft invites need your attention). The badge goes away when the count reaches zero. While Outlook isn't running, it keeps the last count, because the meetings still wait for you.

items.text:

Rescan emails from the last 24 hours… works like this:

items.title: Quick checks
items.text:
1. Look at the tray icon and hover over it. The tooltip says what is wrong.
  2. Open Settings, Connection and press Test connection.
  3. Ask Claude to run index_status. It reports whether Outlook is running and how far indexing is.
  4. Open the logs: tray menu, Open log folder.

items.title: Outlook is not running
items.text: The icon is grey with ! and the status line says "Outlook is not running". Start classic Outlook, or use the tray's Start Outlook. Indexing resumes by itself. Searches against the existing index keep working meanwhile; reading a message that isn't indexed yet, attachments, drafts and calendar tools need Outlook.

items.title: Outlook is open but Clippy says it isn't running
items.text:
• Run both at the same elevation. Neither should run as administrator.
  • It must be classic Outlook, not the new Outlook.
  • After an Outlook restart, click into the Outlook window and then another window, or wait a minute. Clippy re-attaches by itself. If it doesn't, restart Outlook.

items.title: Outlook is not responding
items.text: A dialog is open in Outlook, or it is busy. Clippy times out COM calls instead of hanging. Close the dialog in Outlook and try again. The tray shows "Outlook is not responding" and a notice appears if it lasts more than two minutes.

items.title: 401 from curl or Claude
items.text:
The token is wrong or was regenerated. Copy the command from the tray again and re-add the server. Also check Settings, Connection for the port.

A 401 from curl with no token is expected, and tells you the server is up.

items.title: Attachment download fails (attachment_link)
items.text:
What you see Cause and fix curl answers 401 CLIPPY_TOKEN isn't set in that shell, or it is an old token. Press Copy WSL token line in Settings, Connection, put the line in ~/.bashrc in WSL and run source ~/.bashrc. The link isn't used up by a 401. See Set CLIPPY_TOKEN curl answers 404 The link was already used, expired after 10 minutes, or Clippy restarted or changed port. Ask Claude for a new link curl answers 405 Something other than GET was sent. Use the exact curl command from the tool result curl: (7) Failed to connect Clippy isn't running, or WSL isn't in mirrored networking. See Claude can't connect from WSL Too many open download links (10)... Download or wait for open links to expire (10 minutes), then ask again The open download links already hold 200 MB... Same: download the open links or wait for them to expire Too many download links in the last 10 minutes (20). Try again in <n> min. Wait that many minutes The attachment is <n> MB; attachment_link handles up to 100 MB... Use get_attachment to save it on the Windows side Clippy can't use its private download folder. Use get_attachment instead. %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\links\ is a junction or symlink, or its permissions can't be set. Remove the folder (when Clippy is closed) and restart Clippy Outlook errors Same as for other attachment tools: start Outlook, close dialogs

A failed or interrupted download shows as attachment download failed in Activity. More: attachment_link.

items.title: Claude can't connect from WSL
items.text:
• Check %USERPROFILE%\.wslconfig has networkingMode=mirrored under [wsl2].
  • Run wsl --shutdown in Windows and open WSL again.
  • From WSL, curl -i -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp should answer 401.

See Connect Claude Code.

items.title: Test connection messages
items.text: Message What to do The server isn't running Check the tray icon for the reason. Restart the app if needed Nothing answers on 127.0.0.1:port Wrong port, or the app is not running Didn't answer within 5 s The app is busy or blocked. Check the logs Answered without a token Another program uses that port. Pick a different port Rejected the token (401) Regenerate and re-add the server Another MCP server is answering Another program uses that port. Pick a different port

items.title: The port is already in use
items.text: Settings shows "Port N is in use or can't be opened. The server stays on port M." Choose a different port between 1024 and 65535, then run the new claude mcp add command.

items.title: Search finds nothing
items.text:
• The first backfill may still be running. Ask Claude for index_status.
  • The mail may be outside your retention window (12 months by default) or in a folder that isn't indexed. Check Settings, Index.
  • A search with folder="inbox" does not include subfolders.
  • If results look wrong, use Rebuild index… from the tray.

items.title: Rebuild the index
items.text: Tray menu, Rebuild index…, then choose My mailbox or All mailboxes. Clippy deletes its index and reads your mail again, newest first. Your mail is not touched.

items.title: An invite wasn't sent
items.text:
Clippy never sends invites. It saves the meeting unsent in your calendar. Open it from Draft invites in the tray (or from your calendar), add the Zoom or Teams link and send it in Outlook.

  • Check the mode in Settings, Scheduling. Draft only saves the meeting, and Disabled refuses.
  • If a recipient didn't resolve in Outlook, nothing was created.

items.title: An update failed or was rolled back
items.text:
Open About Clippy's Revenge… from the tray menu. Its status line gives the reason, for example ✗ The last update attempt failed: GitHub didn't answer within 15 s. See Updates for how updating works.

  • Couldn't check or download. Usually the network, a proxy or GitHub's rate limit. Press Check for updates later. Clippy retries by itself.
  • The checksum or size doesn't match. The download is deleted and nothing changes. Try again later. If it keeps happening, install with install.ps1.
  • The previous version is still in use. Restart Windows and try again.
  • "v... didn't start on this PC, so Clippy's Revenge went back to v...". The new version didn't start, so Clippy put the old one back. It won't install that version again by itself. Look in the log folder for the reason and wait for a newer release, or press Update now to try again.
  • Clippy shows "Update Clippy's Revenge or rebuild the index" after a rollback. The failed version had already upgraded the index. Choose Rebuild index… in the tray.
  • Clippy doesn't start and ClippysRevenge.exe is missing. Run the install line again, which puts a good copy back:
irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

Your settings, token and index are kept. - Updates keep rolling back and another program permanently uses Clippy's port. A new version confirms itself by starting its server on the port. If that port is taken for good, the update can't confirm and rolls back. Choose a different port in Settings, Connection, then run the new claude mcp add command.

items.title: AI drafts
items.text: See AI drafts for how it works. Open the Activity window first: it says why a mail got no draft.

items.title: No drafts appear
items.text:
• Check that Draft replies automatically is ticked in the tray's AI drafts submenu, and that Settings, AI drafts shows a ready status after Check.
  • If Activity shows AI drafts: Claude isn't signed in, sign in to Claude Code in a terminal (run claude), then press Check in Settings. Clippy never signs in for you.
  • AI drafts: daily limit of <n> reached means the Daily limit is used up. It continues tomorrow, or raise the limit in Settings. Rescans and re-checks of old drafts count too.
  • AI drafts: Claude's usage limit was reached is your Claude plan's limit. Clippy tries again at the time shown.
  • no draft for the email received …: Claude's confidence … is below your minimum means Claude wasn't sure a reply was needed. Select the email in Outlook and use Draft a reply to the selected email, or lower Minimum confidence.
  • Mail that arrived before you turned AI drafts on, mail older than Ignore mail older than (days), mail where you are not in To or CC, newsletters and automatic mail get no draft. See Rules.
  • Drafting waits while Outlook isn't running or indexing is paused.

items.title: Where did my draft go?
items.text: If Clippy's AI draft vanished from Drafts, look in Deleted Items. When a newer message arrived in the thread and the draft was no longer right, Clippy re-checked it. It either replaced it with a new draft or moved it to Deleted Items because no reply was needed any more. The Activity window says which, for example Outdated AI reply draft moved to Deleted Items (no reply needed any more): <subject>. You can drag the draft back to Drafts. Clippy only does this for an AI draft that you haven't edited, opened or sent, and never deletes anything for good. To stop it, turn off Update or remove my AI drafts when a thread moves on in Settings, AI drafts. See Outdated drafts.

items.title: An old draft is still in Drafts after a new one appeared
items.text: Clippy keeps an old draft when you edited it or have it open, and says so in Activity: The old draft is still in Drafts because it was changed or is open. Delete it yourself when you no longer need it. If a move to Deleted Items fails, Activity says AI drafts: an outdated draft couldn't be moved to Deleted Items. It's still in Drafts.

items.title: Rescan emails from the last 24 hours is greyed out
items.text: It needs Outlook running and the email index available. While a rescan runs, the item reads Cancel rescan (d/t) and Draft a reply to the selected email is greyed out. If a click only shows a balloon, read it: There are no emails from the last 24 hours to rescan., Today's AI draft limit (<n>) is used up. or Claude isn't ready: …. A rescan stops early for the reasons in Activity.

items.title: The draft has a placeholder where my Zoom link should be
items.text: Check Facts about you in Settings, AI drafts. not found means the file %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\my-email-context\SKILL.md is missing, larger than 16 KiB or not valid UTF-8: use Edit my facts… in the tray. template only means you haven't written anything outside the <!-- … --> comments yet. Activity shows Facts about you: my-email-context SKILL.md not found or unreadable — drafts go without it. when the file goes away. See Facts about you.

items.title: There is no yellow Clippy: line, or a draft isn't updated any more
items.text: No line: Start each draft with a highlighted note on why it was drafted may be off in Settings, AI drafts, or Claude gave no note for that email. A draft you removed the line from (or changed in any way) counts as edited, so Clippy leaves it alone and never replaces or moves it. That is intended. See The reason line.

items.title: The draft ignored my attachment, or has a yellow Couldn't read … note
items.text:
• Check that Read attachments and synced shared files for drafts is ticked in Settings, AI drafts. If it is off, only file names are sent.
  • Read the note. It names the reason: not synced to this PC (the link doesn't match a file in a library or folder your OneDrive syncs: sync it or add a shortcut), Clippy only opens shared files from people in your organization, password-protected, larger than 25 MB, no text in it, maybe a scan, Clippy can't read .<ext> files, the file seems damaged, it took too long and too much attachment text for one draft. See Why couldn't Clippy read my shared file?.
  • Images, and links that aren't OneDrive or SharePoint links, are skipped with no note.
  • Outlook must be running: with Outlook closed, files that need Outlook are skipped.
  • The Activity suffix (attachments: 3 read, 1 not read) shows how many files were used. It has counts only. The log never names a file.
  • %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\ai-files\ should be empty. If a file stays there, Clippy deletes it at the next start.

items.title: The tray shows tokens unknown or no Today: line
items.text: The line appears only after you gave AI drafts consent. tokens unknown means Claude reported no token numbers for today's calls. See Token tally.

items.title: Clippy never says it noted my edits, or the style has no "Edits I usually make" section
items.text:
Clippy learns from your edits only when all of this holds:

  • Learn from how I edit Clippy's drafts is on in Settings, AI drafts, and you gave consent.
  • The draft was saved after you updated to version 0.1.1, for an email with an internet message id, and did not use attachment text (those are never kept).
  • You sent it as a reply to that email, from your own mailbox, and it still carries Clippy's marker. A reply you wrote from scratch, or a draft you made with a tool, isn't matched.
  • Clippy has synced your Sent Items since (it checks at most every 5 minutes, after a sync), and it is within 30 days.

The section appears after the next writing-style update (Regenerate, or the weekly one) once at least 3 edited drafts with text exist. Drafts you sent unchanged only raise the "unchanged" count, so they don't count toward the 3. If you edited your style skill yourself, an automatic update leaves it alone: use Regenerate. Clippy shows AI drafts: noted how you edited <n> sent drafts. in Activity when it finds some.

items.title: The writing style isn't there yet
items.text: Clippy builds your writing-style skill from your sent mail, and waits until your Sent Items are indexed. Sent Items are indexed before the Inbox, so it normally appears early in the first backfill: finishing Sent Items wakes the drafting worker, which builds the skill if Draft replies automatically and Update weekly are on. Check progress with index_status or the Activity window (Sent: backfill complete). Until then, drafts have no personal style. If Activity says writing style not updated: only <n> sent emails (need 20), there is too little sent mail yet: Clippy tries again after 24 hours, or press Regenerate… in Settings when you have more. An edited skill is never overwritten without asking.

items.title: Logs
items.text: Logs are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippysRevenge\logs, one file per day (clippy-YYYYMMDD.log), kept for 7 days. To get more detail, set Log level to Debug in Settings, General. It applies at once.

items.title: Start over
items.text: Run the uninstaller with -Purge (see Install) and install again. This deletes your settings, token and index, so you will need to add the server to Claude Code again.

items.title: Updates
items.text: Clippy's Revenge can keep itself up to date. Once a week it asks GitHub whether a newer release exists and, by default, installs it the next time it starts. You choose how much it does by itself.

items.title: The three modes
items.text:
Set the mode in the tray's Settings…, General, Updates. It applies at once. All settings are listed on the Settings page.

Mode What Clippy does Install automatically (default) Checks weekly, downloads and verifies a newer release, and installs it at the next start, without asking Only tell me Checks weekly and shows a balloon when a newer release exists. It downloads and installs nothing unless you press Update now in the About window Don't check Never checks by itself. You can still check by hand in the About window, and update with install.ps1

Cautious? Pick Only tell me

The default installs new versions without asking. If you want to look at a release before it runs on your PC, choose Only tell me, read the release notes, and press Update now when you are ready. See the trust model for why this can matter.

items.title: How and when it updates
items.text:
• Only the installed copy updates itself: the one in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ClippysRevenge\, put there by install.ps1. A copy you run from Downloads or a build folder never checks, downloads or installs anything by itself.
  • The first check runs about a minute after Clippy starts, in the background, so start-up never waits for the network. A check is due when the last successful one is at least 7 days old. While Clippy runs, it looks again every 6 hours. A failed attempt is not repeated for 24 hours.
  • Only full releases count. A pre-release is ignored. A release is installed only when its version is strictly newer than the one you run, so Clippy never downgrades.
  • With Install automatically, Clippy downloads and verifies the new ClippysRevenge.exe in the background. The install itself happens at start-up: right at the next start, or at once when the check runs during the first 30 minutes after a start and Clippy is idle. A check later in a long session only downloads and verifies. Clippy then shows a balloon that the update installs the next time it starts. Press Update now in the About window to do it sooner.
  • The swap is quick: Clippy renames the running exe to ClippysRevenge.exe.old, puts the new exe in place, shuts down, starts the new one and exits. The new instance shows a balloon, "It looks like I got an upgrade. I'm now v...", and deletes the .old file. Clippy starts nothing else during an update. It never runs install.ps1, a shell or any script.
  • Sync and the first backfill may be running when the swap happens. They stop with the app and resume after the restart. Your settings, token and index are not touched by an update.

items.title: What is sent to GitHub
items.text:
Nothing about you. Clippy sends plain, unauthenticated GET requests, with no cookies and no sign-in, to three kinds of address:

  1. Release lookup: https://api.github.com/repos/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest
  2. Downloads: ClippysRevenge.exe and SHA256SUMS.txt from the release on https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/download/<tag>/. GitHub redirects these to its own download servers. Clippy follows at most 5 redirects and only to github.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com or objects.githubusercontent.com. Anything else fails the download.
  3. Nothing else. No analytics, no telemetry, no crash reports.

Each request carries a few standard headers: User-Agent: ClippysRevenge/<your version>, an Accept header, and for the lookup GitHub's API version header. That is all. Your mailbox, the index, your settings and your PC's name are never sent. GitHub sees your IP address, as any website does. Windows proxy settings apply, and the HTTPS certificate checks are never relaxed.

The lookup times out after 15 seconds, and the download has a size limit and a time limit. GitHub's unauthenticated API allows 60 requests per hour per IP address, which a weekly check never gets near, but a busy office network might.

items.title: The About window
items.text:
Right-click the tray icon and choose About Clippy's Revenge…. Settings, General, Check now opens the same window and starts a check. It shows:

  • the version, with the commit when known, and the .NET and Windows versions
  • where Clippy runs from: Installed in <folder>, or Running from <folder>. Only the installed copy updates itself.
  • the mode: Updates: install automatically, Updates: only tell me or Updates: don't check
  • Last checked: never, or the date and time with how long ago it was
  • a status line: Checking for updates…, Downloading v0.0.7… 42 %, Verifying the download…, You have the latest version., v... is available (released ...)., or v... is downloaded. It installs the next time Clippy's Revenge starts, or press Update now. If something failed, it says why, after a ✗, for example ✗ The last update attempt failed: GitHub didn't answer within 15 s. A check you started yourself says ✗ Couldn't check for updates: ...

Buttons and links:

  • Check for updates looks up the latest release at once, in any mode. It downloads nothing.
  • Update to v... (or Update now) downloads, verifies and installs the newest release, then restarts Clippy by itself. It waits up to 2 minutes for Clippy to finish what it is doing. It works in every mode, but only for the installed copy. If Clippy is busy, it says so, and you can try again in a minute.
  • Documentation opens this manual. Release notes opens the page of the latest release on GitHub.

A copy that isn't installed can still check by hand. It then points you to the release page instead of updating itself.

items.title: If an update goes wrong
items.text:
Clippy verifies a new version before it installs it, and it can undo an install.

  • Checks before installing. The download must be exactly the size the release lists, its SHA-256 must match the one in the release's SHA256SUMS.txt (and the one GitHub lists for the file), it must be a Windows program, and its version must match the release. If any check fails, the file is deleted and nothing changes.
  • Rollback. After the swap, the old process waits up to 60 seconds for the new one to confirm that it started. If the new exe crashes, exits or never confirms, the old exe is put back and started again. You see the balloon "It looks like v... didn't start, so I went back to v.... I won't install v... again." Clippy skips that version until a newer one is released. Update now in the About window can still try it.
  • Index too new. If the failed version had already upgraded the index database, the older version can't open it and shows an error. Use Rebuild index… in the tray.
  • The exe is missing. If something went wrong badly enough that both exes are gone, run install.ps1 again. See Troubleshooting.

The Activity window lists every update event, such as update check: v... available, update check: up to date (v...), update v... downloaded and verified, installing update v..., updated from v... to v..., update v... didn't start; back on v... and update failed: .... The log has the details.

items.title: Releases
items.text:
Every change that reaches the project's main branch is published as a new GitHub release, v<version>, with ClippysRevenge.exe, install.ps1 and SHA256SUMS.txt. What changed is in the changelog and in the release notes. A version with a suffix (such as 0.2.0-beta) is a pre-release. Clippy's updater ignores pre-releases, and install.ps1 installs the latest full release.

Only the newest releases are kept on GitHub: the latest three, plus the newest one that is at least three days old when all three are younger than that. Older releases and their tags are deleted. So you can only go back to a recent version.

items.title: Update by hand
items.text:
Run the install line again. It always installs the latest release, whatever the mode, and works even when Clippy can't update itself:

irm https://github.com/dirkpetersen/clippys-revenge/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

See Install or update. To go back to an older version, download that release's ClippysRevenge.exe and run .\install.ps1 -Source .\ClippysRevenge.exe. Clippy never downgrades by itself.

items.title: Trust model
items.text:
An update is trusted because of two things: it comes over HTTPS from the project's GitHub release, and its SHA-256 matches the SHA256SUMS.txt published in that same release. That proves the file is the one published in the release and arrived intact.

It does not prove who published it. The checksum comes from the same place as the file, so it can't tell you that the publisher is who you think it is. Anyone who could publish a release in the project's GitHub repository (a stolen account or access token, a compromised build workflow) could publish an exe with a matching checksum, and installed copies in Install automatically mode would install it within a week without asking.

The exe is also not code-signed yet (see Security). Windows SmartScreen shows its warning for a file you download in a browser, but not for a file Clippy downloads and installs itself, so there is no prompt at update time.

If that risk is too high for you, choose Only tell me or Don't check, and review each release before you install it with install.ps1.

items.title: Turn updates off
items.text: Settings, General, Updates: pick Don't check. Clippy then makes no network connection for updates at all, until you press Check for updates in the About window.
